author: adjudication
purpose: Reconciles the three independent Studio UI design proposals into one design, resolves their contradictions with reasons, folds in the After Effects teardown that none of them had, and applies operator decisions SAD-006 (panels un-merge) and SAD-007 (full video and VFX in scope). Authority stays in Master Spec section 14 and the WP-KERNEL-STUDIO contracts.
naming_law: STU-SECTION-003: no vendor product name is a Studio menu, tool, panel or command name. Vendor names appear here ONLY as capture provenance.

one_vocabulary.why: The three proposals use three names for several of the same things. This design uses one name per concept throughout. Every microtask authored from this file must use these names.

The single evaluation deciding whether an element applies right now

contradictions_resolved.topic: Does every tool appear in the menu, and in what shape?
contradictions_resolved.menu_says: YES. proposal.analysis.divergences[Tools in the menu bar]: 'PUT EVERY TOOL IN THE MENU under WORKSPACE > Tools (1,270 registry-expansion leaves). No source suite does this.' Corrected downstream to 353 after adopting the tools rebuild. Rationale: OUI-006 makes the menu the exhaustive index, and [STU-MDL-006] forbids capabilities with no model path, so a menu node gives every tool a stable command_id and AccessKit author_id at once.
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: The rail is the tool home. proposal.tool_palette_model.visible_at_rest: '20 visible slots must reach 353 tools. They cannot and must not try. Roughly 120 tools live in the rail's groups; the remaining ~230 are reached by context, search or family browse.'
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: tools is one of the 75 panels (always_relevant class) occupying the left-rail region; it takes no position on menu presence.
contradictions_resolved.is_it_a_real_conflict: Partly false. The tools proposal's own discoverability.surfaces[Menu bar] says 'the menu is the complete projection; anything absent from the menu is a registry bug.' Both authors therefore agree every tool must be menu-reachable. The genuine disagreement is about menu SHAPE, and about which surface is the tool's primary home.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Every tool appears in the menu, and NOT as a flat list. WORKSPACE > Tools > <family> > <tool>: 22 family submenus, 362 leaves, mean 16 leaves per family, max 44 (filter_live). The rail is the primary home for the ~120 core tools; the menu is the index; search and family browse are the other two projections. All four dispatch the identical command id.
contradictions_resolved.reason: The menu proposal already made this exact argument about a different node and then failed to apply it to its own: analysis.per_app_menu_shape[aftereffects].shape_finding says 'Any single Studio Effects menu that lists effects flat is unusable; the family level is mandatory.' 362 tools is the same problem as 635 effects. The tools proposal supplies the family level: family_grouping_notes.why_21 says 21 families is 'browsable in one screen, which 353 is not.' Using the families as the menu structure satisfies the menu proposal's index promise and the tools proposal's browsability requirement with one artefact.
contradictions_resolved.consequence: WORKSPACE > Tools becomes an expansion node whose leaf_source is the tool registry's 22 families, not a registry query. Its count is asserted (362), not budgeted, because it was rebuilt from per-app sources. It is one of only two expansion nodes in the tree exempt from carried_gaps CG-04.

contradictions_resolved.topic: How is availability gated? Three different context vectors, two different valuations.
contradictions_resolved.menu_says: Gate on a document capability PROFILE, never on a document type. context_gating.document_capability_profile.why_not_a_type_enum: 'A type enum would re-create the seven-application silo inside one binary and would break [STU-DOC-004].' The predicate `requires` is a conjunction over 8 clause kinds (container, layer_kind, doc_feature, selection:>=N, selection_kind, tool, capability, mode). TWO-valued: enabled or disabled, with 9 machine-readable disabled_reason codes.
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: Gate on a context vector whose first field IS document.kind, an 8-value enum (raster, vector, layout, motion, video, web, photo_catalog, whiteboard). THREE-valued: AVAILABLE / INAPPLICABLE_HERE / NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT. three_valued_result.why_three_not_two: 'Two-valued availability forces a choice between clutter and mystery. The middle state is where discoverability actually lives, and it is the state a persona toggle destroys.'
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: Gate on document_types, 'a hard pre-filter; a panel not declared for the active document type never enters resolution', plus a can_bind runtime veto that is absolute and applied before priority.
conflicts: (a) TYPE vs PROFILE. The tools and panel proposals both key on a document type enum; the menu proposal states in terms that such an enum rebuilds the seven-application silo. The menu proposal is right on the operator's own evidence: OUI-004 exists precisely because the same capability serves multiple document shapes.
(b) TWO-VALUED vs THREE-VALUED. The menu is 2-valued; the tools proposal is 3-valued and its third state means HIDDEN in the rail, which collides head-on with menu rule_1_nothing_is_ever_hidden.

(c) HIDE vs EMPTY-STATE for panels. The panel proposal sets hide_when_unbound default false and renders an explanatory empty state, agreeing with the menu; but its own panel_classification[document_type_specific] says such panels are 'absent - not merely collapsed - for the others', agreeing with the tools proposal instead. The panel proposal contradicts itself.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: ONE predicate, evaluated ONCE per element per context change, THREE-valued, over the document PROFILE. The three-valued result renders differently per surface, and the difference follows from what each surface is rather than from a compromise.

resolution_detail.input: The document profile: a set of declared container kinds {artboard, page_spread, timeline, board, site_tree} plus a set of feature flags. It is declared at creation from a document preset and GROWS when a container or layer of a new kind is added; it never shrinks silently. The tools proposal's document.kind and the panel proposal's document_types are re-expressed as profile predicates, e.g. document.kind==video becomes container:timeline AND doc_feature:footage_clips. The seven named shapes survive ONLY as (1) creation presets that seed a profile and (2) the layout persistence key, per CR-08.
resolution_detail.note_on_clause_kinds: This is the menu proposal's 8 clause kinds plus the four fields the tools proposal's context vector carried that the menu proposal lacked (color_mode, capability_flags, selection.count, task_scope). document.has_timeline and document.page_count are dropped as redundant: has_timeline IS container:timeline, and page_count is a selection/document query, not a gate.

states.INAPPLICABLE_HERE: Predicate false AND the host can name one action that would make it true. Carries reason_code + unavailable_reason + remedy_command_id.
states.NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT: The element has no meaning for this profile at all and no single action reaches it. Carries reason_code + the profile clause that owns it.

resolution_detail.reason_code_provenance: The first 9 and the last are the menu proposal's list, plus WRONG_COLOR_MODE and CAPABILITY_FLAG_ABSENT from the tools context vector, plus EXPRESSION_DRIVEN which the After Effects fold-in requires (see CR-19 and integrated_design.numeric_control).

per_surface_rendering.menu: AVAILABLE enabled; INAPPLICABLE_HERE greyed with reason and remedy; NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT greyed with reason. NEVER hidden, at any level, including top-level titles. Menu rule_1 wins here because the menu is the index and the AccessKit address space; a hidden node has no stable target and Argus cannot inspect what is not rendered ([STU-MDL-002]).
per_surface_rendering.tool_rail: AVAILABLE enabled; INAPPLICABLE_HERE dimmed with the remedy inline; NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT absent from the rail. The tools rule wins here because the rail carries ~20 slots against 362 tools and is explicitly not an index.
per_surface_rendering.search_and_palette: NEVER filters on availability. Sorts on it, displays the reason. Enforced by tools R-04: 'The user types a correct tool name, gets nothing, and concludes Studio does not have the tool. That is strictly worse than the persona toggle, because a persona at least tells you which mode to switch to.'
per_surface_rendering.panels: AVAILABLE docked or rail-registered; INAPPLICABLE_HERE renders an explanatory empty state (hide_when_unbound false); NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT not in the dock BUT still emits studio.rail.<region>.<panel> so an agent can always discover and open it. This is the panel proposal's own determinism_requirement, applied to resolve its own internal contradiction (c).
per_surface_rendering.context_bar: Single-occupant; only AVAILABLE candidates enter the slot resolver.

resolution_detail.promotion_is_the_remedy: The menu proposal's rule_4_enable_by_promotion_not_by_refusal and the tools proposal's INAPPLICABLE_HERE remedy button are the same mechanism described twice. Unified: every INAPPLICABLE_HERE state carries remedy_command_id, and the menu renders it as an enabled sibling leaf while the rail and tooltip render it as an inline button. Worked example from the menu proposal: in a page-layout document MOTION > Keyframes is INAPPLICABLE_HERE with NO_SUCH_CONTAINER, and DOCUMENT > Timelines > New Timeline is the enabled remedy. Worked example from the tools proposal: Node tool on a pixel layer is INAPPLICABLE_HERE with WRONG_LAYER_KIND and 'Convert this pixel layer to curves?' is the remedy.
resolution_detail.the_slot_resolver_is_not_a_competitor: The panel proposal's contextual_binding_rule is a SEPARATE stage that runs after availability and only over AVAILABLE candidates. It decides which panel occupies a single-occupant slot. Both stages exist and are named distinctly: availability predicate (per element, three-valued) then slot resolver (per slot, ranking). The panel proposal's can_bind veto stays as an absolute veto inside the resolver, applied before priority, exactly as specified.

contradictions_resolved.evidence: Dreamweaver ships the mechanism this resolution generalises: 48 of 85 toolbar items carry enabler_js, 15 carry showif_js, 57 carry dom_required, 64 carry update_event, and 60 of 60 property inspectors implement canInspectSelection. The field precedent is ENABLEMENT predicates plus a separate binding declaration, which is exactly the two-stage split above. The 012 shell already ships the enablement half: effective_disabled(cmd, ctx) and editor_menu_command_enabled(command_id, ctx) with EditorMenuEnableContext, tested by editor_menu_commands_gated_by_active_target_context.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Do disabled items grey or hide?
contradictions_resolved.menu_says: VISIBLE AND GREYED, ALWAYS, at every level including top-level titles. Never hidden. Answers the operator's still-open question with a position.
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: Three-valued; NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT is hidden from the rail. Its OQ-03 explicitly leaves the menu question to the operator and asks whether INAPPLICABLE_HERE is product-wide or palette-only.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: hide_when_unbound defaults false 'because a tab that vanishes breaks muscle memory and breaks an agent's ability to address it', but document_type_specific panels are 'absent'.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Per CR-02's per_surface_rendering. The menu never hides anything. The rail hides only NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT, and search still returns it with its reason. Panels never vanish from the AccessKit tree even when undocked. Answering tools OQ-03 directly: INAPPLICABLE_HERE is a product-wide concept, not a palette-only one.
contradictions_resolved.reason: This is not a compromise between the three; it falls out of what each surface is. A menu is an index and an address space, and an index whose entries disappear is not an index. A rail is a 20-slot ergonomic surface over 362 tools and was never an index. A panel dock is an arrangement, and the AccessKit tree is the address space behind it, so the dock may omit what the tree must still carry.
contradictions_resolved.operator_status: This remains listed in operator-ui-requirements.json open_for_operator_decision and studio-architecture-decisions.json still_open_for_operator. Recorded here as a recommendation with its reason, not as a settled decision.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Distinct panel count: 814 vs 75 vs 84.
contradictions_resolved.positions: Capability registry kind==panel yields 814 rows. Panel proposal dedup yields 75 distinct panels plus 9 reused shell panes, with an honest_caveat that rejecting any of five internal-mode merges raises it by at most 17. SAD-006 rejects one of those five and states 75 rises to roughly 84. Menu proposal sizes WORKSPACE > Panels at 84.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: 814 is WRONG and must not be cited. 75 is superseded. 84 is the correct pre-After-Effects, pre-video baseline. The integrated count is 90.
contradictions_resolved.reason: The 814 figure is the GRD-001 defect plus string-derived non-panels; the panel proposal states it inspected the bucket and found rows such as 'Top', 'Underline', 'Visible', and deliberately did not use it as the dedup input. contradictions_resolved.topic: After Effects effect corpus: 481 effects in 36 categories, or 635 in 46.
contradictions_resolved.who_said_what: Menu proposal analysis.per_app_menu_shape[aftereffects].totals_cited and EFFECTS menu rationale both cite 481 effects / 36 categories / 2,001 enumerated option lists / 338 plugin binaries / 208 effects with typed parameter records / 1,573 typed parameter records. The tools proposal cites 481 effects, 1,573 typed records, 833 hard bounds, 618 soft, 378 differing (61.2%), 2,001 enumerated option lists, 74 GROUP_START/END pairs, 294 COLLAPSE_TWIRLY, 980 defaults, 499 precisions, 72 units, 54 display units, 359 of 481 support_urls resolving to 24 distinct manual pages.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: 635 effects in 46 categories is right. 481/36 is a stale read of an earlier revision of the same file, and the effects catalogue's generated_at (05:26:34Z) is after the menu proposal's (05:20:46Z), which is the mechanical explanation.
corrections_that_change_a_design_decisio: enumerated option lists: 2,001 is wrong. Three separate figures now exist and must not be conflated: 157 parameters carry an option list, 422 option lists were recovered across the string pools, and 1,047 option strings sit on parameters. The ParamSpec.options field is fed by the 157.

soft bounds: 618 is wrong, it is 606; differing is 366 not 378; 60.4% not 61.2%. The tools proposal's ARGUMENT is unaffected and remains correct: a control that knows only one range would be wrong more often than right, and hard/soft must be separate fields from the first commit.

support_url denominator: 359 of 635 is 56.5%, not 74.6%. More importantly the distinct page count is 225, not 24. That is an order of magnitude, and it matters: 225 distinct vendor manual anchors is a serious seed for UiDescriptor.manual_anchor, where 24 would have been near-useless.

GROUP_START/GROUP_END are param TYPES (codes 13 and 14 in param_type_enum), not flags. COLLAPSE_TWIRLY and CANNOT_TIME_VARY are flags (bits 0x20 and 0x2). The tools proposal treated all four as one class; the generator must read two different fields.
CANNOT_TIME_VARY count was never stated. It is 327, so ParamSpec.keyframable is true for 1,246 of 1,573 (79.2%). That number sizes the keyframe work directly.
contradictions_resolved.effect_on_the_menu_tree: EFFECTS was budgeted at 1,230 registry-expansion leaves against 481 AE effects. With 635, of which 106 are preset-only pseudo-effects that belong in a preset browser under the menu proposal's own OQ-7 rule, the effect list is 529 AE entries in 46 categories. The family level stays mandatory. Net addressable-item change from this correction alone is +48.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Are After Effects workspaces captured? The motion default layout was extrapolated from Premiere.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: coverage_gaps[aftereffects] labelled EXTRAPOLATED_NOT_CAPTURED: 'AE panel placement in the motion default layout below is therefore extrapolated from Premiere's dvaui workspace evidence ... NOT from an AE workspace file.' Its OQ-6 asks whether an AE workspace capture should be added before the motion layout is treated as settled.

Panel OQ-6 is CLOSED by data.
contradictions_resolved.what_the_extrapolation_got_right: Timeline is the entire lower branch of the outermost splitter in 16 of 16 workspaces. Full-width bottom time dock confirmed, matching Premiere's Timeline CENTRE-BOTTOM 16/18.

what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.claim: The panel proposal put effect-controls in the RIGHT dock at 55% height and explicitly rejected Premiere's placement: 'Premiere's own legacy placement co-tabs Effect Controls with the Source Monitor (LEFT 5, CENTRE-TOP 4), but its modern Properties2 placement is right, and a keyframe editor needs height, which the right dock has and the centre-top stack does not.'
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.measured: AE Default and AE Standard both co-tab 'AE Effect Controls' with 'AE Project' in the TOP-LEFT frame. AE Effects (the workspace) leads the same frame with Effect Controls active. That is Premiere's so-called legacy placement, shipped by the vendor of record for motion in its own default.
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.why_the_justification_fails: The stated reason was that a keyframe editor needs height. In After Effects the keyframe editor is NOT Effect Controls - it is the Timeline, which is the full-width bottom band. Effect Controls is only the parameter list. Once the keyframe timeline exists as its own surface, the height argument evaporates.
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.resolution: For the composition (motion) profile, effect-controls docks LEFT, co-tabbed with project-bin. For the sequence (video) profile it stays RIGHT, because Premiere is the vendor of record there and Premiere's clip keyframes live inside Effect Controls rather than in the sequence timeline. Two profiles, two placements, both now grounded rather than extrapolated. This difference is itself part of the evidence for CR-20.

what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.claim: motion right_rail visible with audio-meters, on the reasoning 'Premiere shows MiniAudioMixer in every workspace that has audio.'
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.measured: All 16 AE factory workspaces declare HasLeftBar=false, HasRightBar=false, HasStatBar=false, HasToolBar=true. After Effects ships no side bars at all, and its Audio panel (AEGP_AudioPal) is a right-dock TAB in Default, Standard, Animation, Essential Graphics and Color.
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.resolution: Meter Rail hidden by default for the composition profile, with audio-meters as a right-dock tab. Meter Rail visible for the sequence profile (Premiere MiniAudioMixer far-right rail in 16 of 16 placements, the only 100% placement fact in the corpus).

what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.claim: motion left dock group1 = [project-bin, effects-browser, media-browser, library, preset-library, markers].
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.measured: AE Default puts the effects BROWSER ('AE Effects Palette') in the RIGHT group with Properties, Align and Audio, not on the left. Standard, Animation, Effects, Essential Graphics and Color all place it right too.
what_the_extrapolation_got_wrong.resolution: effects-browser moves to the Inspect Dock for the composition profile. It stays in the Browse Dock for the sequence profile (Premiere Effects browser LEFT in 8 of 11 placements).

contradictions_resolved.corroboration_gained: HasToolBar=true in 16 of 16 AE workspaces adds a fifth vendor to the Context Bar evidence, which previously stood at Photoshop 8/8 anchor=top control-bar, Illustrator ControlBar 12/12, Affinity's single tbar and InDesign's 34 Control Panel variants.
contradictions_resolved.counterexample_gained: HasLeftBar=false in 16 of 16 means After Effects is a COUNTEREXAMPLE to the left Tool Rail: its 27 tool commands live in the top toolbar. The rail still stands at 3 of 5 vendors with placement evidence (Premiere Tools left rail 18/19, Photoshop anchor=left 8/8, Dreamweaver left panelframe width=35 in both shipped workspaces), and AE's tool set is 27 commands where Studio's is 362, which is why a horizontal strip suffices there and cannot here. Recorded honestly rather than suppressed; the rail is user-movable per OUI-005 and a Layout Preset may relocate it into the Context Bar.

contradictions_resolved.topic: What is the layout persistence key, given that the document type enum is refuted?
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: Layout is PER DOCUMENT TYPE with a per-tab override and a named-preset layer. effective_layout = L3 ?? (selected L1 preset) ?? L2 ?? L0, keyed by document_type. Reasoning: 'Not one of the 50 captured workspace files is project-scoped.'
contradictions_resolved.conflict: CR-02 removes document_type as a field. The cascade needs a key.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: layout_key = profile signature = the sorted set of the document's declared CONTAINER kinds. Not the feature flags. The L0..L3 cascade is preserved unchanged and simply re-keyed.
contradictions_resolved.reason: Containers are what the layout is actually about: a timeline needs a bottom dock, a page_spread needs a pages panel, a site_tree needs a file tree. Feature flags are far more volatile - a profile grows the moment a layer of a new kind is added - and keying on them would swap the operator's arrangement mid-edit. Containers change rarely and change meaningfully.
contradictions_resolved.consequence: Adding a timeline to a page-layout document changes the layout key from {page_spread} to {page_spread,timeline}. That is correct: it is the menu proposal's rule_4 promotion made visible. But it MUST be an offer, not a silent swap, because the panel proposal's R-2 (inspector thrash) applies with more force to a whole-layout change. The transition is operator-confirmed once per document and then remembered.
contradictions_resolved.collision_note: raster, vector and photo share the signature {artboard}, so the container set alone is insufficient to separate them. The tie-break is the dominant feature flag: pixel_canvas+channels -> raster, vector_network -> vector, raw_develop+catalog_link -> photo. This is the one place a feature flag enters the key, and it is stated explicitly rather than left to implementation. A document carrying two of the three resolves to whichever preset created it, recorded on the document.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Scrub control fine modifier: Alt or Ctrl. Each proposal disqualifies the other's key by name.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: rule_6_modifiers: 'Shift = coarse, step x10. Alt = fine, step x0.1. Shift+Alt = x0.01. Alt is chosen for fine rather than Ctrl because Ctrl is a menu accelerator prefix and OUI-006 makes the menu load-bearing; and because Alt-drag-to-duplicate is a CANVAS gesture, so it cannot collide with a field gesture under rule 1.'
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: 'Shift coarse x10, Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) fine /10, Shift+Ctrl x100, Alt NOT a magnitude modifier. Alt is already the duplicate / subtract-from-selection / sample-alternate modifier in every one of the captured applications. Overloading it for step magnitude guarantees collisions inside canvas gestures.'
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Fine = Ctrl. Coarse = Shift. Shift+Ctrl = x100. Alt is excluded. Shift+Alt = x0.01 is dropped.
contradictions_resolved.reason: The panel proposal's objection to Ctrl is defeated by the panel proposal's own rule_1_claim_at_press: 'The topmost widget under the pointer at PRESS-DOWN claims the gesture for its entire duration. There is no movement threshold, no ambiguity window and no hand-off.' A menu accelerator can only fire when no widget owns the pointer, so Ctrl held during an owned scrub gesture cannot reach the menu. Meanwhile the tools proposal's objection to Alt is not defeated by anything, and the After Effects capture strengthens it further: Alt is load-bearing in exactly the surface where scrubbing matters most. AE binds Alt+W, Alt+Shift+A/F/L/M/P/R/S/T (the eight add-keyframe-at-current-time commands), Alt+LeftArrow, Alt+Right Arrow, Alt+Shift+LeftArrow and Alt+Shift+RightArrow, all in the timeline. Giving Alt a second meaning as a step magnitude in the same surface is the collision the tools proposal predicted.
kept_from_the_panel_proposal: modifiers sampled continuously during the gesture, not latched at press
the accumulated value does not jump when the magnitude changes, because accumulation is in value space
Escape aborts and restores the pre-press value, discarding the transaction rather than committing a no-op

at a screen edge the cursor is HIDDEN and delta continues to accumulate, restored at the press point on release; deliberately NOT OS cursor warping, because warping is fragile on multi-monitor Windows and moves a pointer the out-of-process inspector is tracking
contradictions_resolved.operator_status: OUI-008 lists the exact keys as a proposal item and both proposals raise it as an open question (panel OQ-11, tools OQ-02). Recommendation recorded with both reasons; operator decides.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Hover cursor on a scrub field.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: rule_3 forbids exactly that: splitters use CursorIcon::ResizeHorizontal / ResizeVertical, scrub fields use CursorIcon::ResizeColumn, 'If that reads too similarly in practice, the scrub field takes a custom cursor - but the two must remain visually distinct', plus an 8px inset between a field's hit rect and any splitter hit strip.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Panel wins on the cursor: fields use ResizeColumn, splitters use ResizeHorizontal/ResizeVertical, 8px inset. Tools wins on the second cue: add the 2px gutter tint on hover.
contradictions_resolved.reason: The panel proposal identified a collision the tools proposal did not see, and the collision is real because OUI-008 requires the field to advertise draggability with a resize cursor while a dock splitter wants the same affordance. The tools proposal's gutter tint is not redundant: it is the only cue that works on a pen or touch device where there is no hover pointer at all, and the panel proposal has no equivalent. Take both halves.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Wheel over a dense panel.
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: 'The field CONSUMES the wheel event so the surrounding panel does not scroll while the pointer is over a ScrubValue.' No mitigation offered.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: Same consume rule, plus the problem it creates: 'In a dense panel, most of the surface IS fields, so an unqualified wheel-over-field-steps-value makes the panel nearly unscrollable. This is a genuine conflict, not a hypothetical: Illustrator's Transform panel is 240x298 and is almost entirely fields.' Mitigation: a reserved 10px scroll lane on the inner right edge containing no field, plus wheel over any label, group header or blank area scrolls.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: Adopt the tools consume rule AND the panel mitigation. The inversion (wheel scrolls, modifier+wheel steps) stays as panel OQ-12, a one-line default change if the lane proves too narrow in the visual debugger.
contradictions_resolved.reason: Not a real contradiction, an omission. The panel proposal did the work the tools proposal skipped, and OUI-008 states the wheel behaviour as a requirement, so the mitigation must preserve it rather than qualify it.

contradictions_resolved.topic: AccessKit role for a numeric field: when is it a Slider rather than a SpinButton?
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: 'Role::SpinButton for a bounded scalar; Role::Slider where the parameter's captured metadata declares a slider range DISTINCT FROM its edit range.'
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: 'Slider where a soft range EXISTS, SpinButton otherwise.'
contradictions_resolved.size_of_the_disagreement: 606 After Effects parameters declare both a hard and a soft range; 366 of them differ. The two rules therefore disagree on 240 parameters in the After Effects corpus alone.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: The tools rule: a soft range exists -> Slider.
contradictions_resolved.reason: The accessible role should describe the INTERACTION available, and a soft range means a drag range exists whether or not its two numbers happen to coincide with the hard range. A role that flips when a vendor capture is refreshed and two bounds coincide is unstable, and instability in a role is exactly what breaks an out-of-process inspector's assertions across capture revisions.

contradictions_resolved.topic: author_id grammar. Two incompatible schemes.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: studio.<kind>.<region>[.<name>][#<instance>]. Examples: studio.tab.right.3.layers, studio.group.right.1, studio.split.right.1, studio.field.transform.x, studio.panel.preset-library#2.
conflicts: A numeric field has two different addresses: studio.field.<panel>.<parameter> versus studio.panel.<panel>.<param-path> / studio.options.<tool>.<param>.

The panel grammar embeds the REGION and the GROUP ORDINAL in the id (studio.tab.right.3.layers), which does not survive a dock reorganisation - the exact defect the panel proposal itself criticises in tab_bar.rs: 'tab_bar.rs addresses tabs by INDEX (tab-{pane}-{index}), which shifts under reorder; Studio panel tabs should be addressed by NAME instead.'
contradictions_resolved.resolution: The tools grammar, with three additions lifted from the panel proposal.
rules: An author_id NEVER contains a region, a group ordinal or a tab index. studio.tab.right.3.layers becomes studio.tab.layers; its region and group are PROPERTIES on the AccessKit node, not part of its id. This applies the panel proposal's own stated principle consistently to its own grammar.

A numeric field is addressed by its OWNER, not its location: studio.panel.<panel>.<param-path> when it lives in a panel, studio.options.<tool>.<param> when it lives in the Context Bar Tool Zone. One field, one id, unchanged if the panel moves docks.
Charset [a-z0-9-.] only, kebab-case within a dotted path, no locale text, no vendor branding, never derived from position, sibling index or label text.
stable_id = 'hs-' + author_id with dots replaced by hyphens, derived mechanically and never authored twice. studio.tool.draw-path.pen -> hs-studio-tool-draw-path-pen.
An id, once shipped, is never reused and never renamed; a rename adds a new id plus an aliases[] entry and the inspector accepts either.

Register the 'studio.' prefix in accessibility/registry.rs DECLARED_HASHED_AUTHOR_ID_PREFIXES; derive egui::Id from the author_id string so Studio lands in egui's hashed space, disjoint by construction from the small fixed NodeId band (10-13, 20-22, 30, 31, 40-43, 50-56, 60-67, 80-90, panes at 100+). Studio must NOT consume fixed ids, because its panel and tool counts are dynamic.
kept_from_the_panel_proposal: #<n> instance suffix, first instance unsuffixed so existing addresses never change when a second is opened.
studio.dock.state - a JSON projection of the whole dock model, so a GUI regression test is a string comparison rather than a screenshot diff.
studio.slot.<slot>.resolved - the author_id the slot resolver chose plus the matched selector and the winning priority.
studio.gesture.active - the author_id owning the pointer plus the gesture kind (scrub | tab-drag | panel-drag | splitter | pan | none).
contradictions_resolved.why_those_three_are_kept: They are the highest-value observability affordances in any of the three proposals and the tools proposal has no equivalent. Without studio.gesture.active, a test asserting 'a drag from inside a field did not move the panel' must infer ownership from the absence of an effect. Without studio.slot.resolved, an agent must infer the resolver's decision from what happens to be visible.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Is the horizontal bar tool-driven or selection-driven?
contradictions_resolved.tools_says: Options Bar, TOOL-driven: 'The whole bar is replaced by that tool's modal parameters', contents_order = tool identity chip, tool preset picker, the tool's declared controls, overflow disclosure, reset-to-default. Hard cap 12 interactive controls.
contradictions_resolved.panel_says: Context Bar, SELECTION-driven single-occupant contextual slot resolved against slot='context-bar'. Its five worked examples resolve to a character-attributes bar, an object-geometry bar, a multi-select alignment bar, a clip trim bar - and only the no-selection case resolves to 'active-tool options (binds_to tool:<current>)'.
contradictions_resolved.the_captures_split_the_same_way: Photoshop options bar, Illustrator control bar and Affinity context toolbar are tool-driven. InDesign's Control panel and Dreamweaver's 60 property inspectors are selection-driven; the tools proposal itself records InDesign's behaviour as 'The control panel switches on what is selected (object vs text vs table vs frame), not on which tool is active' and notes 'InDesign already separates what the tool will do from what the selection is, and puts the second on the shared bar.'
contradictions_resolved.resolution: ONE region, TWO zones, split by the rule the tools proposal already stated for a different purpose.
contradictions_resolved.the_rule: tool_options_surface.two_surfaces_one_rule: 'If changing the value changes what the tool will DO NEXT, it belongs in the Options Bar. If it changes what is ALREADY on the canvas, it belongs in the Properties panel.' Apply that same test to the bar itself.

contents: the tool's declared controls in declared order
tool_zone.collapses_to: the identity chip alone when the tool declares no options
tool_zone.evidence: Photoshop anchor=top content=control-bar with panelid.static.options in 8 of 8 workspaces; Illustrator ControlBar 12 of 12; Affinity's single tbar; After Effects HasToolBar=true 16 of 16.

selection_zone.driven_by: the slot resolver over slot='context-bar' against the current selection
selection_zone.evidence: InDesign ships 34 resource variants of ONE Control Panel chosen by what is selected, plus numbered variant families Alignment 14, Paragraph 13, Style 10, Character 9, Transform 6, Text Wrap 6, Pages 6. Dreamweaver ships 60 property inspectors into one slot, 60 of 60 declaring {tag, attrname, priority, selection, hideclass}.

shared.overflow: grouped flyout, never truncation, per Affinity's [Tool settings flyout] and [Tool settings flyout group heading] contexts; Affinity's own worst case is 81 context-toolbar strings on the Select tool alone, and it solves that with a grouped flyout rather than truncating
shared.cap: 12 interactive controls per zone; a tool declaring more than 30 becomes a Properties-panel citizen and mirrors only its top 3 in the Tool Zone
shared.never_a_tab_stack: No vendor with a workspace capture stacks tabs on the top edge.

contradictions_resolved.reason: The two proposals are answering two different questions and both questions are real. Splitting the region into zones costs nothing structurally, is grounded on both sides of the capture split, and preserves the panel proposal's single-occupant discipline within each zone.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Three names for one thing: task mode, workspace, named preset.
contradictions_resolved.settled_upstream: The adjudication brief resolves menu OQ-8 as a false conflict: [STU-UNI-002] says switching mode 'changes tool prominence and panel layout only; document state, selection, colour and history are untouched' and that Studio adopts 'the shared-primitive architecture, not an app-switching shell'. That is a layout preset, not the whole-UI swap OUI-004 rejects.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: ONE concept, ONE name: Layout Preset. Menu location WORKSPACE > Layout Presets. It supplies (a) dock arrangement, (b) Tool Rail order and pinned groups, (c) search ranking bias. It supplies NO gate of any kind.
contradictions_resolved.reason: All three proposals independently arrived at the same non-gating rule and only the names diverged. Menu rule_3: mode 'MUST NOT change which menu items exist, which are enabled, or where they sit.' Tools workspaces_are_ranking_hints: 'A workspace supplies a rail ordering, a set of pinned groups, a panel layout, and a search ranking bias. It supplies no gate.' Panel L1 named_preset is 'the vendor workspace concept, but scoped to a type so it can never swap the whole application.'
contradictions_resolved.enforceable_test: tools R-11, adopted verbatim as an inspector assertion: for any Layout Preset W and any element E, availability_state(E) must be identical with W active and with W inactive.
contradictions_resolved.naming_evidence: 42 shipped workspaces across four vendors (Affinity 9, Illustrator 12, Premiere 19, Dreamweaver 2) and now 16 more from After Effects: 58 total. Every single one is named for a JOB or a TASK - Retouching, Colour Grading, Typography, Compositing, Tracing, Printing and Proofing, Color Analysis, Metalogging, Motion Tracking, Paint, Text, Essential Graphics, Effects, Animation, Review, Minimal. Not one is named for a persona, a discipline or an application mode. Studio's shipped presets use job names.
contradictions_resolved.scope: The panel proposal's L1 layer, keyed by profile signature per CR-08.
contradictions_resolved.do_not_collapse: Task Scope is a different mechanism and keeps its own name: a scoped, deliberately entered and deliberately exited tool-plus-options set. Photoshop ships three (Select and Mask 8 tools / 15 properties, Content-Aware Fill 6 tools / 5 properties, Neural Filters 5 tools) as taskspace / taskspace-tool / taskspace-property elements in its .kys. A Task Scope narrows the visible tool set and swaps the Tool Zone; it never swaps panels, menus, shortcuts or chrome, and it always has a visible exit.

contradictions_resolved.topic: The menu proposal contradicts itself on its own item count: 4,600 or 6,247.
contradictions_resolved.evidence: proposal.totals and proposal.sizing_against_reality.studio_total_addressable_items both state 4,600 (1,533 explicit + 3,067 expansion). But sizing_against_reality.honest_reading says 'Studio's 6,247 items', R-2 says '6,247 items is a maintenance surface', R-3 says 'at Studio scale it is 6,247', and R-9's honest_statement says 'Do not treat 6,247 as a committed item count. Treat 1,533 as designed and 4,714 as budgeted' - and 1,533 + 4,714 = 6,247, not 4,600.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: 4,600 is the figure carried forward. 6,247 is a stale figure from an earlier revision of the same file that survives in the prose and in three risk entries but no longer matches the totals block or the per-menu table (which sums to the 4,600 decomposition).
contradictions_resolved.caveat: BOTH numbers are upper bounds. Only 1,533 explicit leaves are asserted; 3,067 are budgeted from registry queries and inherit GRD-001 wholesale except the two nodes independently rebuilt (Tools 362, Panels 90). See carried_gaps CG-04.
contradictions_resolved.after_effects_adjustment: +48 from the effect corpus correction (529 non-pseudo AE effects against the 481 budgeted). Separately, the AE menu capture converts several NOT_CAPTURED absorption claims into real leaf lists; that raises confidence, not the count.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Shortcut arbitration was computed without After Effects.
contradictions_resolved.menu_says: shortcut_policy.the_measured_problem.method: 'InDesign ships 162 shortcut CATEGORIES but no key values, so it is excluded from the collision counts. After Effects has no shortcut capture.' Union of 448 distinct chords across Photoshop 146, Illustrator 235, Premiere 277, Dreamweaver 185; 211 contested, 18 agreeing, 193 in conflict; 18 chords frozen as an immovable spine.
contradictions_resolved.measured: aftereffects_commands_shortcuts.json ships 673 keyboard bindings across 32 contexts, 651 joined to a command label, 665 labelled commands in 31 categories, stored as literal text so no key decoding was needed. Two malformed entries are disclosed by the capture itself.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: The 448-chord union, the 211/18/193 split and the 18-chord frozen spine are all PROVISIONAL and must be recomputed with After Effects folded in before any default set is frozen. This is a named prerequisite, not a caveat.

conflicts_already_visible_without_recomp.detail: Ctrl+P is one of the 18 frozen chords (Print). After Effects binds it to ToolPin, the Puppet tool, in the CEggAppTool context. This is the first measured contest of a frozen chord. Proposed handling: the freeze holds, Print keeps Ctrl+P globally, and Puppet takes a canvas-context binding. Recorded because a frozen spine that is breached silently is worse than one that was never frozen.

AE ToolPen=G with Shift+G cycling the pen/mask-feather group. Photoshop and Illustrator both use G for Gradient, and the menu proposal's bare-letter ruling gave G to Gradient on a 2-of-3 vote. AE makes it 2-of-4 for Gradient with a live objection. Rank-3 (one letter one tool) still gives G to Gradient; AE's Pen keeps P, which AE does not otherwise claim.
AE ToolRotate=W; Photoshop W is the magic-wand/quick-selection group.
AE ToolPan (Pan Behind / Anchor Point)=Y; Photoshop Y is the History Brush.
AE ToolMask (Shape/Mask cycle)=Q with Shift+Q backward; Photoshop Q is Quick Mask.
AE ToolCamera=C with Shift+C cycling; Photoshop C is Crop, which is one of the eight tools present in five source applications.
AE CompToggleEffects=E (double-tap reveals expressions); Photoshop E is the Eraser.
AE CompToggleUberAnimatingKeyframes=U (double-tap reveals modified properties); Photoshop bare U is the shape-tool group.
AE PrevKeyframe=J and NextKeyframe=K, with Shift+J / Shift+K scoped to selected layers. Photoshop J is the healing-brush group.
AE ToolPaint (Brush/Clone/Eraser)=Ctrl+B. The menu proposal ruled Ctrl+B to Bold on a 2-of-4 vote. AE is a fifth claimant and it is a tool, not a text attribute.
AE ToolText=Ctrl+T. The menu proposal ruled Ctrl+T to Free Transform. AE agrees with Illustrator that Ctrl+T is type-related, which changes the vote from 1-of-4 to 2-of-5 against the ruling.

The menu proposal reserved function keys for panel toggles and dropped Photoshop's F2/F3/F4. After Effects binds F9=EasyEase, Shift+F9=EasyEaseIn, Ctrl+Shift+F9=EasyEaseOut, Shift+F2=DeselectAllKeyframes and Shift+F3=ToggleGraph (Show/Hide Graph Editor). Five keyframe commands now claim function keys. The reserve rule survives at GLOBAL scope only; all five bind in the timeline context, which rank-2 (context scope before arbitration) already permits.

AE binds 1/2/3 to the orbit/pan/dolly camera tools and 4/5/6 to the 3D position/scale/rotation gizmo modes, with Ctrl+Shift+1 for the legacy wireframe gizmo. Studio's frozen spine contains Ctrl+Shift+0 and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+0; bare digits were unclaimed and are now claimed by a document-shape-specific surface.

contradictions_resolved.what_survives_unchanged: Rank-2 (context scope before arbitration) absorbs most of this. After Effects contributes 32 contexts, which is comparable to Premiere's 31, and confirms rather than challenges the context-first architecture. AE's own Shift+letter cycling confirms rank-3's cycling half.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Re-apply the SAD-006 test to the other proposed merges.
contradictions_resolved.the_test: SAD-006 principle_established: 'A consolidation that only works given an unbuilt capability is not a consolidation, it is deferred debt. Merge only where the merged panel is usable as-is.' Operational form: does the merge require two of its members to be VISIBLE AT THE SAME TIME?

verdicts.merge: InDesign's 34 Control Panel resource variants -> 2 Studio panels (context-bar, effect-controls); 43 captured surfaces total counting the 9 XP*PanelViews
verdicts.reason: The 34 variants are 34 alternative layouts of ONE slot, chosen by what is selected. Only one selection exists at a time, so two variants can never be simultaneously relevant by construction. This is not a merge at all in the sense SAD-006 rejects; it is the contextual-slot mechanism itself, and it is the single largest piece of evidence in the corpus that the field ships exactly this.
verdicts.the_nine_effect_views_checked_separately: The 9 XP*PanelViews (BevelEmboss 1125 nodes, DropShadow 1005, DirectionalFeather 950, InnerShadow 940, Satin 610, InnerGlow 600, OuterGlow 550, GradientFeather 550, Feather 365) are nine effect-KIND layouts inside one Effects surface. The vendor itself shows one editing pane at a time beside a checkbox list, and Photoshop's Layer Style dialog is the same shape. An effect STACK with several effects on one layer is a list of collapsible groups in one scroll, not two panels - which is how both Premiere Effect Controls and After Effects Effect Controls already work, with After Effects shipping 74 GROUP_START/GROUP_END pairs and 294 COLLAPSE_TWIRLY flags to drive exactly that. No multi-instance capability is required.

verdicts.merge: Premiere's 5 Titler surfaces (TitlerProperties, TitlerStyles, TitlerTools, TitlerActions, TitlerEditor) plus Graphics -> graphics-templates = 1
verdicts.reason_1_simultaneous_visibility: Applying a style from a style browser to a title while watching its properties change requires TitlerStyles and TitlerProperties visible at once. That is precisely the swatches-plus-gradients situation SAD-006 rejected, and it fails the test for the same reason.
verdicts.reason_2_category_error: The merge folds surfaces of three different KINDS into a panel. TitlerTools is a tool set and belongs in the Tool Rail, not in a panel. TitlerEditor is an on-canvas editing mode and belongs in the Viewport. Neither is a panel at all, so calling this a six-to-one panel collapse mis-describes what is happening.

correct_decomposition.studio_home: the properties panel occupying the inspector slot, via a binding - not a new panel
the Tool Rail; the type and shape tools already exist among the 362
an on-canvas editing mode of the Viewport, not a panel

verdicts.net_panel_count_effect: Unchanged at 1 (graphics-templates already exists in the 84). What changes is the claim: this was never a six-to-one merge, it is a distribution to five existing homes plus one panel. Four of the six surfaces move to homes that already exist and one leaves the panel domain entirely.
verdicts.corroboration: After Effects models the same job the same way: AEGP_Capsules (Essential Graphics) is ONE panel, and its character, paragraph, align and properties surfaces are separate panels co-tabbed with it in the Essential Graphics workspace - AEGP_PropertiesPal, AEGP_Info, AEGP_AudioPal, AEGP_TimePal, AE Effects Palette, AEGP_Align, Design Libraries, AEGP_CharacterPalette, AEGP_ParagraphPalette, AEGP_TrackerPalette, AEGP_Filler in one 11-tab group. The vendor of record for motion graphics keeps them separate.

verdicts.merge: Photoshop's swatches/gradients/patterns/customshapes/styles/toolpresets/brushpresets and 5 more -> preset-library = 1 (12 vendor surfaces)
verdicts.note: Carried through unchanged. Panel count 75 -> 84. The panel proposal's own R-1 had already stated the condition: 'Multi-instance support is a HARD requirement of the merge, not an enhancement. If multi-instance slips, un-merge the panel before shipping.'

verdicts.merge: 13 Photoshop and Illustrator type surfaces -> 5 panels (character, paragraph, text-styles, opentype, glyphs) plus tabs-indents
verdicts.reason: This IS the un-merged form: five separate panels, not one. The collapse is across vendors, not across jobs. Corroborated by After Effects, which also ships character and paragraph as two separate panels (AEGP_CharacterPalette, AEGP_ParagraphPalette), co-tabbed in the Text workspace.

verdicts.merge: Illustrator SeparationPreview + FlatteningPreview, InDesign InkMgrPanel + ColorPanel(PrintUI), Affinity soft-proof and 32-bit preview -> print-preview = 1
verdicts.reason: These are mutually exclusive rendering previews of the same document. Showing two at once is not a workflow; the operator is either separating, flattening, ink-managing or soft-proofing.

verdicts.merge: Dreamweaver's 60 property inspectors -> properties = 1 plus 60 binding declarations
verdicts.reason: Same argument as the InDesign Control Panel: one selection, one winning binding. This is the slot resolver, not a merge.

verdicts.merge: source-viewer (the panel proposal's internal-mode caveat list, member 1)
verdicts.verdict: SURVIVES, conditional on the centre tree
verdicts.reason: A professional editor needs Source and Program simultaneously - Premiere's EDITING workspace ships them side by side and 8 of its workspaces containing both place them that way. But the centre Viewport is an UNBOUNDED egui_tiles tree per OUI-002, so two viewers are two editor groups, not two tabs of one panel. Simultaneous visibility is already available with zero new capability. The condition is that the centre tree exists, which is prerequisite P-03 regardless.

Colourists routinely want waveform and vectorscope at once, so the merge would fail the test if the scope kind were a single-choice selector. It does not, because the vendor already solves it INSIDE the panel: Premiere's and After Effects' Lumetri Scopes panel renders several scopes simultaneously in one internal grid. That is a panel-internal layout, not a dock multi-instance capability, and it is buildable as-is. Requirement recorded: the scopes panel must ship its internal N-up grid in the same microtask as the panel, not as a follow-up, or the merge silently becomes deferred debt.
TOC, index, cross-references, conditional text and bookmarks are sequential jobs, not simultaneous ones.
Covered above under the InDesign verdict. A stack of collapsible parameter groups is the vendor model in Premiere, After Effects and InDesign alike.

verdicts.merge: NEW, arising from After Effects: AEGP_MotionSketch + AEGP_Smoother + AEGP_Wiggler -> keyframe-assistant = 1
verdicts.reason: All three operate on the keyframes of a selected property and are never needed simultaneously: Motion Sketch records position by dragging, Smoother reduces keyframes, Wiggler adds noise. Adjacency evidence alone would not be enough after SAD-006, but the simultaneous-visibility test passes independently. Adjacency is nonetheless present: the three are consecutive tabs in ONE frame of the AE Animation workspace, alongside AEGP_PropertiesPal, AEGP_Info, AEGP_TimePal, AE Effects Palette and AEGP_AudioPal.

verdicts.merge: NEW, arising from After Effects and SAD-007: clip timeline + keyframe timeline -> one panel with two modes

contradictions_resolved.summary: Of the five merges the panel proposal flagged as carrying an internal mode selector, one is rejected (preset-library, by SAD-006) and four survive, with scopes carrying an explicit in-scope requirement. Of the two the operator named for re-examination, the InDesign Control Panel collapse survives and the Premiere Titler collapse is rejected and redecomposed. One new merge arising from After Effects survives and one is rejected.

contradictions_resolved.topic: The scrub control has no state for an animated or expression-driven value.
contradictions_resolved.who_missed_it: All three. OUI-008 describes a value control over a static number. Neither the tools proposal's ScrubValue interaction_contract nor the panel proposal's value_field_contract has a state for 'this value is a function of time' or 'this value is computed by an expression'.
contradictions_resolved.why_it_matters_now: In After Effects almost every numeric field is both scrubbable and keyframable. Measured: 1,246 of 1,573 typed effect parameters (79.2%) are keyframable, being those without the CANNOT_TIME_VARY flag; and any property can be replaced by an expression, stored as an `expr` chunk of NUL-terminated UTF-8 on the value stream.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: ParamSpec.keyframable stays as the tools proposal defined it (static, generated as the inverse of CANNOT_TIME_VARY). A NEW runtime field, TemporalState, is added; it is per-property-per-document and is not part of the ParamSpec. Full design in integrated_design.numeric_control.
contradictions_resolved.consequence_for_carried_gap_CG_02: The tools proposal's R-14 already blocks ScrubValue on UiTreeNode gaining numeric_value / numeric_min / numeric_max / numeric_step / unit. After Effects widens that: the node must ALSO carry temporal_state, time and keyframed_at_time, or a GUI test asserting a scrub result on an animated property is unfalsifiable, because the reported numeric_value is a function of the playhead rather than a stored constant. Same defect class, larger surface.

contradictions_resolved.topic: Is the clip timeline the same panel as the keyframe timeline?
contradictions_resolved.raised_by: SAD-007, which makes both first-class and asks the question directly.
contradictions_resolved.resolution: TWO panels, one shared time model, defaulting to two tabs in ONE bottom group with a different active tab per profile.
contradictions_resolved.reason_1_the_vendors_disagree_because_th: After Effects ships ONE time surface: the AE Timeline panel holds the layer stack, each layer's property tree, the keyframe tracks and the graph editor, and the Graph Editor is a MODE reached by ToggleGraph (Shift+F3), bound in the CCompCompCmd and TLOutlinePano contexts. There is no separate graph-editor panel among the 28 panel ids in the 16 factory workspaces. Premiere ships TWO: the sequence Timeline for clips and tracks, and a keyframe strip inside Effect Controls - which is why 'effectcontrols' is one of Premiere's ten largest command namespaces at 54 commands. The difference is not stylistic. An After Effects row IS a layer property; a Premiere sequence row is a track containing clips and has no property tree.
contradictions_resolved.reason_2_the_SAD_006_test: A merged single panel with a mode switch forces one-at-a-time with no escape, and the escape would require multi-instance support that does not exist - the exact preset-library situation. A professional editor trimming a clip while shaping that clip's opacity ramp needs both. Two panels give the escape for free, because the dock already permits up to 4 groups per edge.
contradictions_resolved.reason_3_why_the_default_is_still_one_gr: Both vendors ship one visible time surface by default. Two panels means the operator CAN place them side by side; it does not mean Studio should. Default: bottom group 1 holds [timeline, keyframe-timeline] as tabs. For the sequence profile timeline is the active tab; for the composition profile keyframe-timeline is active.
contradictions_resolved.reason_4_why_the_graph_editor_is_NOT_a_t: It passes the SAD-006 test where the timeline split fails it. The graph editor replaces the keyframe strip for the SAME selected properties at the same time; the two views are alternatives, never simultaneous. The vendor gives it a toggle, not a panel, and gives that toggle a shortcut in the timeline's own context. Merge stands.

pointer_gesture_arbitration.why_it_is_here: OUI-008 makes every numeric field a press-and-drag target. A dense panel is therefore a grid of drag targets inside a drag-target tab, inside a drag-resizable dock, next to a pannable canvas. Four gesture consumers, one pointer.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_1_claim_at_press: The topmost widget under the pointer at PRESS-DOWN claims the gesture for its entire duration. No movement threshold, no ambiguity window, no hand-off. A drag beginning inside a field can never become a panel drag, a tab drag, a canvas pan, a dock resize, a marquee or a scroll. Implemented as Sense::click_and_drag(); no other widget may call ctx.set_dragged_id during an active gesture.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_2_drag_chrome_only: Panel and tab drags may START only from the tab, the group title strip or the panel header. Never from the panel body. This removes the conflict structurally rather than dynamically, and it is what every captured vendor does.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_3_splitters_are_separate_strips: DIVIDER_THICKNESS 4.0 visual, DIVIDER_HIT_THICKNESS 8.0 interactive, adopted unchanged from split_layout.rs. Splitters use CursorIcon::ResizeHorizontal/ResizeVertical; ScrubValue uses CursorIcon::ResizeColumn plus a 2px gutter tint on hover. A field's hit rect is inset 8px from any splitter hit strip. See CR-10.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_4_drag_leaves_the_panel: Once a field owns the gesture, motion is tracked in SCREEN space. The value keeps updating when the pointer leaves the field, the panel, the dock or the window. While a field owns the pointer: no other widget shows a hover state, no drop target activates, no tooltip fires, no auto-scroll, no dock resize, no canvas pan. Escape aborts and restores the pre-press value, discarding the transaction rather than committing a no-op. At a screen edge the cursor is HIDDEN and delta continues to accumulate, restored at the press point on release - deliberately NOT OS cursor warping, which is fragile across multi-monitor Windows and moves a pointer the out-of-process inspector is tracking.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_5_wheel: The wheel over a hovered field steps that field's value and the field CONSUMES the event. Every dense panel reserves a 10px scroll lane on its inner right edge containing no field, and the wheel over any label, group header, separator or blank area scrolls. See CR-11.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_6_modifiers: Shift = coarse x10, Ctrl = fine /10, Shift+Ctrl = x100. Alt is NOT a magnitude modifier. Modifiers sampled continuously, accumulated in value space so the value never jumps. See CR-09.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_7_undo: One undo entry per GESTURE. Press opens a transaction on undo_stack.rs; all motion coalesces into it; release commits one entry naming the parameter and its before/after values. Consecutive wheel notches on the same field coalesce, closed by a 400ms idle timeout, by the pointer leaving the field, by focus loss, by a modal opening or by Escape. An AccessKit SetValue is one discrete entry taking the identical clamp and commit path as the drag.
pointer_gesture_arbitration.rule_8_observability: studio.gesture.active is an AccessKit node whose value is the author_id of the widget owning the pointer plus the gesture kind (scrub | tab-drag | panel-drag | splitter | pan | none). A test asserting 'a drag from inside a field did not move the panel' is then two string reads, not a screenshot comparison.

panel_density_model.vendor_anchor: Illustrator declares a preferred docked size on 49 surfaces: median width 240, mode 240 (30 of 49), minimum 130, maximum 490. Character 240x188, Transform 240x298, Align 244x172, Pathfinder 240x107, Stroke 240x31, Swatches 240x111. 240px is the field-tested floor for a dense parameter panel, measured rather than estimated.
panel_density_model.scrub_allowance: Field body minimum 72x24px. 24px is the practical minimum pointer target for a press-and-drag grab; a vendor-era 20px row is fine for click-to-type but too thin to grab reliably. A vendor field body is roughly 56px, so the scrub minimum adds about 16px per field and about 32px for a two-field row.
panel_density_model.derived_floor: 240 vendor floor + 32 scrub allowance = 272, rounded up for a scrollbar gutter and the 10px scroll lane = 300px right dock default, 260px hard minimum.
panel_density_model.row_budget: At 300px: 266px usable. One labelled scalar per row (label 96 + gap 8 + field 72 = 176) or one label plus two linked scalars (24 + 72 + 8 + 72 = 176) for X/Y and W/H pairs. THREE fields on one row does not fit at 300px and must not be attempted. Row pitch 24 + 4 = 28px. A right group at 34% of a 900px column is 306px, minus a 26px tab strip and 8px padding leaves about 9 rows - which agrees with Illustrator's own declared 298px Transform panel height.
panel_density_model.below_minimum: Below 260px the panel switches to a stacked compact form - label above field, one field per row, 20px pitch. It never clips and never hides controls; a panel that would clip shows a horizontal scroll rather than a truncated field.
panel_density_model.wide_format_rule: A panel declaring preferred_width above 320 is registered in its edge but presents as an OVERLAY or FLOATING panel by default. Eight Illustrator surfaces exceed 320: AdobeAltGlyphsPanel 404, AdobeHorizontalTabPanel 430, AdobeFlatteningPreview 490, Stock Unified Content 400, CCX Commenting 350. The vendor does not force these into its own 240 dock and Studio must not either.
panel_density_model.mixing_rule: Do not stack a FIELD-DENSE panel (transform, character, paragraph, effect-controls, adjustments, stroke) with a LIST-DENSE panel (layers, swatches, library, project-bin) in a group under 300px tall. Field-dense panels want a fixed modest height; list-dense panels want all the height they can get.
panel_density_model.after_effects_stress_case: The keyframe-timeline is neither field-dense nor list-dense: it is a two-column panel whose left column is a tree and whose right column is a time graph. It is excluded from the mixing rule and gets its own sizing contract in after_effects_surfaces.

variant_disclosure.verdict: REJECT the timed long-press as the only path to a variant. Keep an untimed, visible disclosure. Long-press survives as a muscle-memory alias with identical behaviour and is never load-bearing.
why: A timed press is an invisible gesture with a hidden duration; nothing on screen states it exists or how long it takes.

It costs the long-press latency on every variant switch.
Adobe itself ships two untimed alternatives - Shift+key cycling and the tool preset picker - which is an admission that the flyout alone is insufficient.

population_pipeline: A build-time generator reads the green-room captures and emits UserManualToolEntry, UserManualAnchor and UserManualPage seed rows, a generated Rust id enum, and tooltip-gaps.json.
UI code names an id from that enum. It never types a display string, a range, a unit or a tooltip. A missing id is a COMPILE error, not a runtime blank.
Where a capture supplies text it is used verbatim with spelling normalised, tagged extraction_method parsed or resolved.
Where no capture supplies text, summary is null, the id is written into tooltip-gaps.json, and L1 renders without the sentence. Nothing is invented.
Handshake-only elements get authored text in the SAME file with extraction_method handshake_authored, so authored versus derived stays countable.
Regeneration is idempotent and diffable: a capture refresh produces a reviewable diff rather than a silent behaviour change.
data_contract.why_the_generator_emits_manual_rows_dire: The UserManual store already has a per-tool row type, a per-anchor row type, a content_hash on every row, a manual_version stamp, a freshness comparator and a deterministic seed path. Making the descriptor and the manual row the same generated record means 'the manual is updated in the same change as the behaviour' holds by construction. With 362 tools and 14,681 parameters, hand-seeding is not viable and CX-982 is otherwise unsatisfiable. Target the canonical user_manual store at USER_MANUAL_VERSION 2.0.4 backed by SurrealDB user_manual_* tables - NEVER the declared-deprecated model_manual shim at MANUAL_VERSION 1.5.0, whose entries would not appear in /usermanual/search, /usermanual/tools or the freshness comparator while every governance check still passed.
ci_gates: Every widget call site's author_id exists in the descriptor set, enforced by the generated enum.
Every descriptor has a non-empty display_name.
Every descriptor's manual_anchor resolves to a real UserManual section.
Every UserManual section is referenced by at least one descriptor - no orphan documentation.
No literal string may reach the tooltip or AccessKit API: the helper signatures accept the id enum, not &str, so this is a type error rather than a lint.
For every kind==param descriptor: hard bounds present OR bounds_unknown explicitly true.
For every kind==param descriptor: format(accessible_value) == rendered_text.

NEW: for every kind==param descriptor, soft_min and soft_max are present as fields even where they equal the hard bounds. 366 of the 606 After Effects parameters declaring both would get the wrong drag range if the pair were collapsed.
tooltip-gaps.json count does not increase between builds without an explicit waiver.

accessible_description IS summary, the same field read twice, never copied.
The tooltip renderer and the AccessKit node builder both take a &UiDescriptor; neither accepts a string literal because the API has no such signature.

numeric_control.name: ScrubValue
numeric_control.principle: ONE widget instantiated from a ParamSpec. The call site names an id and nothing else: ScrubValue::new(ids::STUDIO_OPTIONS_PEN_WIDTH). Every bound, step, unit, precision, default, option list and keyframability comes from the generated spec, so nobody types a range twice and the control cannot drift from the reference application.

interaction_contract.hover: Cursor becomes CursorIcon::ResizeColumn, distinct from a splitter's ResizeHorizontal/ResizeVertical, plus a 2px gutter tint for pen, touch and hover-suppressed contexts.
interaction_contract.click_without_movement: Under 3px of movement within the press enters text edit and selects all. Enter or Tab commits, Escape reverts to the pre-edit value, blur commits.
interaction_contract.press_and_drag: Continuous scrub in screen space. Both axes contribute: delta = dx - dy, so right and up both increase. Summing rather than axis-locking means a diagonal drag works and there is no discontinuity when direction changes.
interaction_contract.wheel: Steps by step_default with no click required; the field consumes the event. Panel scroll is guaranteed by the 10px lane and by wheel-over-label.
interaction_contract.modifiers: Shift coarse x10, Ctrl fine /10, Shift+Ctrl x100, Alt excluded. Sampled continuously, accumulated in value space. See CR-09.
interaction_contract.sensitivity: step_default = max(10^-precision, soft_range / 200), so one 200px drag traverses the soft range exactly once. Parameters with bounds_unknown fall back to a magnitude-relative step based on the current value.
interaction_contract.clamping: Always to hard_min / hard_max. Approaching a SOFT bound decelerates the drag and parks there; crossing it requires dragging through a short resistance zone or typing the value. This matters because 366 of the 606 After Effects parameters that declare both bounds (60.4%) have a soft range narrower than the legal one - a control that knows only one range would be wrong more often than right. Reaching a hard clamp shows a visual stop but does not end the gesture, so dragging back returns immediately rather than after re-traversing the overshoot.
interaction_contract.observed_bounds_hazard: bound_provenance == observed means the control does NOT clamp to that bound; it uses the observed range as the SOFT range and leaves the hard range open. Affinity's 32 bounded brush parameter tags are observed across 455 shipped presets, not declared. Clamping to an observed maximum would forbid legal values that simply never appear in a shipped preset - a silent, permanent capability loss that no test would catch. Enforced in the ParamSpec constructor, not by convention.
interaction_contract.formatting: Rendered at ParamSpec.precision with unit or display_unit appended. The PERCENT display flag renders a stored 0..1 as 0..100%.
interaction_contract.undo: One entry per gesture. Press or first wheel notch opens a coalescing scope keyed by author_id; intermediate values update the document live but write into the open scope; the scope closes into one entry on release, on focus loss, on a modal opening, on Escape (which aborts and restores) or 400ms after the last wheel notch. A test drives each exit path and asserts exactly one entry.
interaction_contract.double_click: Reset to ParamSpec.default. Free, because defaults are captured for 980 After Effects parameters, 1,177 Illustrator parameters, 741 Premiere parameters, 84 Lumetri parameters and 140 Photoshop properties.
interaction_contract.secondary_click: Reset to default, copy value, paste value, add or remove a keyframe at the playhead, add or edit an expression, and 'What does this do?' opening the manual anchor.

accessibility.single_path_rule: set_param_clamped(author_id, value, time, intent, source) where source is one of pointer_drag | wheel | text_entry | accesskit | script and intent is one of SetConstant | SetAtTime | CreateKey | RefuseExpressionDriven. All five callers, including the AccessKit SetValue / Increment / Decrement actions, go through this one function, so an inspector's set produces the identical clamp, rounding, single undo entry and change event as a human drag. If any caller has its own clamp, the accessible value and the rendered value will eventually disagree - which is exactly the failure the inspector exists to catch and would then be unable to catch.
accessibility.expression_refusal_must_be_explicit: SetValue on an Expression-driven field is REFUSED with its reason, never silently applied, or the model path and the operator path diverge.
accessibility.grab_rect: The field's AccessKit bounds must be its GRAB rect (72x24 minimum), not its glyph rect, so an inspector computing a click point from the reported bounds lands inside the draggable body.
accessibility.agreement_test: For every numeric descriptor, assert format(accessible_value) == rendered_text, and assert that driving the value through AccessKit yields the clamped expectation and exactly one undo entry. surfaces.reveal_idiom_to_carry: After Effects' single-key reveal is one of its highest-value interactions and no other captured application has it. U shows properties with keyframes; UU (double-tap) shows all modified properties; E shows effects; EE (double-tap) shows expressions; Shift+U and Shift+E extend the selection. The commands are labelled in the capture as 'Show/Hide Properties with Keyframes (Double-Tap)' and 'Show/Hide Effects (Double-Tap: Expressions)', so the double-tap is a declared behaviour rather than an inference. Studio adopts it, and the double-tap must be an untimed alternative as well (a menu leaf and a palette command), for the same reason the tool flyout long-press was rejected: a timed gesture is nondeterministic for the out-of-process inspector to drive.

default_layout_impact_summary: The composition profile's default layout is rebuilt from measured AE data rather than extrapolated from Premiere; five specific placements change (CR-07).
The bottom dock becomes structural rather than optional for two of the eight profiles, and its minimum height rises to 300px because the keyframe-timeline is a two-column panel.
The Meter Rail becomes profile-dependent: visible for sequence, hidden for composition.
Six new panels join the inventory, taking it from 84 to 90.
Two new shortcut contexts are added: graph_editor and expression_editor.
Two new viewer kinds join the centre: footage and layer.
One new tool family joins: camera_3d.
Every ScrubValue in the product gains a TemporalState, whether or not the document has a timeline, because the state is what tells a static field it is static.

task_modes.settled: Menu OQ-8 is a false conflict. [STU-UNI-002] scopes mode switching to tool prominence and panel layout only, with document state, selection, colour and history untouched, and states that Studio adopts the shared-primitive architecture rather than an app-switching shell. That is an Adobe workspace, not the whole-UI swap OUI-004 rejects.

what_it_never_supplies: any change to document state, selection, colour or history
task_modes.enforceable_test: For any Layout Preset W and any element E, availability_state(E) must be identical with W active and with W inactive. Asserted through the inspector, not by convention.
task_modes.scope_key: profile signature (CR-08). A preset for {timeline} is not offered while a {page_spread} document is focused.
task_modes.naming_evidence: 58 shipped workspaces across five vendors - Affinity 9, Illustrator 12, Premiere 19, Dreamweaver 2, After Effects 16 - and every single one is named for a JOB or a TASK. Not one is named for a persona, a discipline or an application mode. Studio uses job names.
task_modes.after_effects_contribution_to_the_set: Animate, Composite and Track come directly from AE's own factory workspace names (Animation, Effects, Motion Tracking), which were unavailable to the three proposals.
task_modes.menu_home: WORKSPACE > Layout Presets. The menu proposal's 9 Task Mode leaves become preset leaves plus Save Layout Preset, Reset Layout and Manage Layout Presets.
task_modes.do_not_confuse_with_task_scope: A Task Scope is a scoped, deliberately entered and deliberately exited tool-plus-options set (Photoshop ships three). A Layout Preset is a named arrangement. They are different mechanisms with different lifetimes and must keep different names.

video_scope_both_ways.status: SETTLED by SAD-007 on 2026-09-04. The operator's words: 'full blown video capabilitie for profesional editors and vfx artists.' The field is retained per the output shape but the branching is retired.

if_in_scope.verdict: THIS IS THE DESIGN. Video is not an additive layer; it is a first-class shape at the same depth as raster, vector and layout.
if_in_scope.spec_effect: [STU-OVR-015] ('video-footage clip-editing out of scope', added in v02.200) is superseded and must be amended. The edit proceeds only on explicit operator instruction through the CX-405/CX-406 Spec Proposal gate using the copy-first versioned bundle path to v02.206; CX-105A does not list KERNEL_BUILDER as a spec-writing role.
