if_out_of_scope.verdict: RETIRED. Recorded only so the decision is auditable and so a later reader does not reconstruct it.
if_out_of_scope.what_it_would_have_removed: MOTION > Edit Actions (15 leaves), MOTION > Tracks (9), MOTION > Captions (8), MOTION > Audio (9), OBJECT > Clip (18 plus submenus) - roughly 60 explicit leaves - plus the 747 video-domain rows, the sequence profile and its default layout, the clip timeline panel, audio-mixer, audio-meters, captions, the Meter Rail's only occupant, the source and program viewer kinds, and the 9 timeline_edit tools.
if_out_of_scope.what_it_would_NOT_have_removed: The composition profile and everything After Effects contributes: the layer property tree, the keyframe timeline, the graph editor, the expression editor, the tracker, the keyframe assistant, the render queue and the 343 motion-domain rows. Compositing was never the contested part; [STU-OVR-015] named footage clip-editing specifically. This is worth recording because it shows the additive-layer framing was already the wrong shape: excluding video would have removed roughly a third of what the After Effects teardown requires, not a clean layer.
if_out_of_scope.why_the_additive_layer_framing_is_abando: A clean additive layer requires the removable part to touch nothing structural. Video does not qualify: it owns a container kind (timeline), a profile signature, a dock region's default occupancy, a shortcut context, a viewer kind pair and a tool family. Designing it as removable would have meant designing every one of those as optional, which is a larger and more fragile commitment than building it.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Replace MODULE_DEFINITIONS[Studio] and retire the snapshot test that pins it
prerequisites_ordered.why: SAD-005 defect 3. Verified 2026-09-04 by extracting the table: Studio's default_tab is PaneType::ModelRuntime and its tabs are ModelRuntime, Swarm, InferenceLab, FontManager, KernelDcc, UserManual. Not one creative surface - it is the LAB entry reordered, ported verbatim from the React MODULE_DEFINITIONS const so a snapshot test could prove no drift from the web source. Switching to STUDIO today opens model-runtime tooling.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Replace with a real Studio definition whose default is PaneType::StudioViewport. The snapshot test pinning it to the React source must be retired in the SAME change or it will fail the correct implementation.
prerequisites_ordered.blocks: Everything. Until this lands, 'the Studio module has focus' is not a stable predicate and the module-menu insertion rule of the integrated menu cannot be implemented correctly.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Replace module-switch tab-list rewriting with a viewport swap over live state
prerequisites_ordered.why: SAD-005 defect 2 and OUI-001. module_tab_list() rewrites the active pane's tab list on module switch as uniqueTabs([default, ...module.tabs, ...existing]). With Studio documents modelled as PaneTypes, switching to Studio and back would destroy the operator's open document set.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Model Studio documents as a SINGLE PaneType::StudioViewport whose content_id carries the document id, so module_tab_list sees one stable tab and Studio's own document tab strip manages the document set independently of the module machinery. Land with P-01: SAD-005 states both must be fixed together because both trace to the same cause, porting the web app rather than designing for the native shell.
prerequisites_ordered.acceptance: A regression test that switches MAIN -> STUDIO -> MAIN with three Studio documents open and asserts all three survive.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Replace the hard-coded 2x2 with an unbounded egui_tiles centre tree
prerequisites_ordered.why: SAD-005 defect 1 and OUI-002. split_layout.rs is a hand-rolled 2x2 (pane-a..pane-d) with SplitWeights{vertical,horizontal}, ported verbatim from app/src/App.tsx including the React field names because the MT-006 acceptance criteria asserted those names by string. Its own module doc already states egui_tiles is the intended engine, and egui_tiles 0.14 with serde is already a dependency. This is a replacement microtask, not a rewrite.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_keep: The clamp discipline, permanently: clamp_split, apply_set_value, SPLIT_MIN 0.2, SPLIT_MAX 0.8, SPLIT_STEP 0.05, DIVIDER_THICKNESS 4.0, DIVIDER_HIT_THICKNESS 8.0, and the Role::Splitter + clamped SetValue convention. Dock arbitration rule_3 depends on the hit thickness.
prerequisites_ordered.acceptance: N groups with tabs, cross-group document drag, serde round-trip.
prerequisites_ordered.scope_boundary: The shell's remaining non-Studio callers of split_layout.rs migrate onto the same tree in a FOLLOW-ON microtask so the two migrations do not block each other; split_layout.rs is deleted when its last caller is gone.

prerequisites_ordered.title: UiTreeNode gains numeric and temporal metadata
prerequisites_ordered.why: Tools R-14, widened by CR-19. UiTreeNode today is { id, author_id, node_id, role, label, value, disabled, actions, bounds, children }. It carries a string value but no numeric minimum, maximum, step or unit, so OUI-008's accessibility clause - that the accessible value, minimum, maximum and unit agree with what the control renders - is not expressible. argus.set_value ALREADY EXISTS and would happily set a value whose clamp the inspector cannot check. Every scrub control would pass CX-503D1 by being clickable while its actual numeric contract went untested.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Additive change to accessibility/snapshot.rs adding numeric_value, numeric_min, numeric_max, numeric_step, unit, and - required by the After Effects fold-in - temporal_state, time and keyframed_at_time, all Option, all populated from the same ParamSpec and document time the control renders from.
prerequisites_ordered.blocks: P-09 (ScrubValue). Hard predecessor, not a follow-up.

prerequisites_ordered.title: GAP-BIND-AFFINITY extraction pass
prerequisites_ordered.why: Tools tradeoff 1 and OQ-04. Serif's .NET resource keys are the neutral English source text plus a bracketed context, e.g. 'Bloom Tool [Tool description]' and 'Apply a soft diffusion of light effect. [Tool summary]'. Nothing in the resource file joins the two, so tool-level bound prose is 0%.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: One further extraction pass over the Serif.Interop.Persona assembly IL, recording which resource keys are loaded by the same type or method. The class that loads a tool's description is the class that loads its summary; that join is in the IL even though it is absent from the string table.
prerequisites_ordered.expected_yield: lifts tool-level mechanically bound prose from 0% to roughly 58% (about 205 of 362) and would also resolve the 143 4CC tool ids the Affinity tool_panel_registry left unresolved.
prerequisites_ordered.blocks: P-06. Must precede the generator because it changes the generator's shape.
prerequisites_ordered.cost: one extraction microtask; the assembly is already decompiled for the string pass

prerequisites_ordered.title: The descriptor generator, the generated id enum, and the UserManual seed rows
prerequisites_ordered.why: CX-982 requires the UserManual to change in the same implementation change as the behaviour, and a Rust guard at atelier/model_manual_merge.rs fails a wired-surface diff without a MANUAL_VERSION bump. With 362 tools and 14,681 parameters, hand-seeding is not viable. Making the descriptor and the manual row the same generated record is the only approach that satisfies the gate at this scale.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: A build-time generator reading the green-room captures and emitting UserManualToolEntry, UserManualAnchor and UserManualPage seed rows into the CANONICAL user_manual store (USER_MANUAL_VERSION 2.0.4, SurrealDB user_manual_* tables), plus the generated Rust id enum and tooltip-gaps.json.
prerequisites_ordered.do_not: Do NOT target src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_manual/. It still compiles, is still path-included by the desktop app, still exports MANUAL_VERSION 1.5.0 and has a CommandReference type that looks like the right target, but it is a declared-deprecated seed input. Entries written there would not appear in /usermanual/search, /usermanual/tools or the freshness comparator, so L2 'what does this do' would resolve to nothing while every governance check passed.
prerequisites_ordered.acceptance: GET /usermanual/tools/:tool_id retrieves a seeded Studio tool.

prerequisites_ordered.title: One descriptor-driven tooltip helper, then migrate the 142 legacy call sites
prerequisites_ordered.why: Tools R-13. The crate today has 142 direct Response::on_hover_text calls across 24 files, no shared helper, and NOTHING sets an AccessKit description anywhere - tooltip text is currently invisible to Argus. Adding Studio tooltips the same way multiplies an existing product-wide defect by the size of the largest module in the product.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: One helper taking the generated id enum, never &str, emitting BOTH the egui tooltip and the AccessKit description from one UiDescriptor; registered in accessibility/registry.rs. There must be no signature that accepts a literal, so hand-written prose is a type error rather than a lint. The existing seed to build on is left_rail.rs fn icon_button, which already passes tooltip text alongside author_id and is one step from taking a descriptor id instead of two strings.
prerequisites_ordered.scope_question: Whether the 142-site migration is in the Studio work packet or a separate shell packet is open question OQ-P. Leaving them means AccessKit descriptions remain absent outside Studio.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Widen AppCommand into the UiDescriptor and derive the menu from it
prerequisites_ordered.why: OUI-006 and menu INV-1..INV-7. The menu bar today is a hand-written MenuId/MenuBarAction pair - 32 variants against 93 commands across three const tables. That divergence is survivable at 93 commands and fatal at 4,600. A parallel STUDIO_COMMANDS registry is the low-friction move and it would let the menu, the palette and the rail disagree.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Add menu_path, menu_order, domain, requires, capability, menu_only, shortcut_id, manual_anchor, provenance, availability and the ParamSpec block. All defaults compatible with the existing entries, so the four command_registry.rs tests are unaffected by additive fields. fn menu_tree() folds all_commands() by menu_path in a second OnceLock; MenuBarAction becomes Dispatch(command_id).
prerequisites_ordered.also: Extract code_editor/symbol_palette.rs fuzzy_match into command_palette.rs as the shared matcher - its own doc comment already designates command_palette.rs as the extraction target - and build a prefix/trigram index in the same OnceLock. filtered_commands() allocates a fresh Vec per call and substring-scans once per frame; at 4,600 that no longer fits the frame budget.
prerequisites_ordered.scope_question: Whether this is Studio scope or a shell packet is open question OQ-Q. It touches three const tables, dispatch_palette_action and the palette filter, and it benefits every module.

prerequisites_ordered.title: ScrubValue with set_param_clamped as the single write path
prerequisites_ordered.why: Every dense panel depends on it, and pointer_gesture_arbitration is only testable once it exists. A scrub control retrofitted into finished panels would have to re-litigate every gesture boundary.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: ScrubValue::new(id) over ParamSpec, with hard and soft bounds as SEPARATE fields from the first commit even where they are equal, and set_param_clamped(author_id, value, time, intent, source) as the single path for pointer_drag, wheel, text_entry, accesskit and script.
prerequisites_ordered.hard_rule: Do not collapse hard and soft into one range. 366 of the 606 After Effects parameters that declare both would get the wrong drag range, and retrofitting a second bound after the widget ships means touching every call site. bound_provenance is required and observed never clamps.
prerequisites_ordered.temporal: TemporalState ships with the widget, not after it. A field that cannot say it is animated cannot be scrubbed correctly in a composition, and adding the state later changes the widget's press-claim behaviour, which rule_1 makes load-bearing.

prerequisites_ordered.title: The five-region dock host
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Context Bar with its two zones, Tool Rail, Browse Dock, Inspect Dock, Meter Rail, Time & Results Dock, plus the centre tree from P-03. One egui_tiles Tree per region. Right dock functional, the other three stubbed. Dividers adopt split_layout.rs's clamp and hit-thickness constants.
prerequisites_ordered.hard_rule: A PanelMoveRequest is applied as a single transaction against the StudioPanelRegistry FIRST, which owns the truth about where every panel is, and the trees are rebuilt from the registry rather than mutating two trees directly. In debug builds the registry asserts every frame that every registered panel appears in exactly one tree. Without this, a cross-tree drag can remove a tile from the source and never insert it into the target, losing the panel.

prerequisites_ordered.title: StudioPanelRegistry plus the 8-panel invariant spine
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: A parallel registry mirroring pane_registry.rs's conventions - Arc<str> ids, BTreeMap for deterministic iteration, stable kebab-case author_ids - but NOT reusing PaneRecord, because a Studio panel has a dock, a group, a tab index, a binding declaration and an optional instance parameter that PaneRecord does not model. Spine: context-bar, tools, properties, layers, colour, swatches, history, info.

prerequisites_ordered.title: The availability predicate and the slot resolver, proven through Argus
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: One three-valued predicate over the document profile (CR-02) plus the slot resolver for slot='inspector' with three bindings, exposing studio.slot.inspector.resolved, studio.gesture.active and studio.dock.state.
prerequisites_ordered.acceptance: Prove end to end through the AccessKit inspector before adding more bindings. A test that selects, deselects and reselects the same node and asserts the emitted tree is byte-identical. A test that presses inside studio.panel.transform.x, moves across the tab strip and a splitter, releases, and asserts studio.dock.state is byte-identical before and after while studio.gesture.active read 'scrub' throughout.
prerequisites_ordered.risk_being_bought_down: The risk in this design is concentrated in three places - the centre tree, the scrub widget and the resolver - and none of it is in the panels. P-03, P-09 and P-12 are the three worth proving with a deliberately small panel set.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Document time model
prerequisites_ordered.why: Required before any time surface. Neither a clip timeline nor a keyframe timeline can exist without it.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: StudioDocument gains the timeline container kind with frame rate, duration, work area, playhead and time display base, shared by every time surface and every viewer.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Layer property tree and keyframe model in the domain layer
prerequisites_ordered.why: This is a handshake_core::studio domain change, not a UI change, and the keyframe-timeline panel cannot exist before it.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: The property tree over the layer graph (13 property group topics, 759 containment edges as the reference shape), the keyframe record {time, in_interpolation, out_interpolation, values and tangents}, the six-value temporal interpolation enum, the 16.667% default ease influence, per-stream bounds, and the static value container.
prerequisites_ordered.constraint: No wgpu, WGSL or GPU dependency may enter handshake_core ([STU-ARC-002]). The boundary stays the six traits.

prerequisites_ordered.title: keyframe-timeline panel
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: The two-column panel: property tree left, keyframe tracks right, movable divider, shared row height and scroll. The reveal idiom (U/UU, E/EE) with untimed menu and palette equivalents. The keyframe navigator as three separate hit targets adjacent to each field.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Recompute the shortcut arbitration with After Effects folded in
prerequisites_ordered.why: CR-17. The 448-chord union, the 211/18/193 split and the 18-chord frozen spine were all computed without After Effects' 673 bindings across 32 contexts. Ctrl+P, a frozen chord, is already known to be contested.
prerequisites_ordered.blocks: Freezing any shipped set. Not the panels, not the docks - only the shortcut freeze.
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Recompute the union across five binding tables, re-derive the frozen spine, re-rule every contested chord under the existing rank 1-9 rules, and add the graph_editor and expression_editor contexts to the precedence order.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Graph editor as a mode of keyframe-timeline
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Value graph and speed graph replacing the time column, toggled by one command. Temporal interpolation only in this stage; spatial interpolation waits on carried gap CG-06.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Expression evaluation and the inline expression editor
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: The expression container on the property stream, evaluation, the error surface with structured fields, the pick-whip, and the inline row editor reusing the shell's code_editor module.
prerequisites_ordered.constraint: MUST reuse code_editor, its keymap and the extracted fuzzy matcher. [STU-SECTION-003] forbids double features and an expression editor would otherwise be a third code surface.

prerequisites_ordered.title: expression-editor panel
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: The task_episodic dockable editor over the same evaluation, with the 333-identifier vocabulary in 12 categories, dual snake_case and camelCase spelling with the modern form canonical.

prerequisites_ordered.title: Clip timeline panel and the trim grammar
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Tracks with headers, clips, transitions, audio lanes, and the 9 timeline_edit tools: ripple edit, rolling edit, slip, slide, rate stretch, razor, remix, track select forward, track select backward.

prerequisites_ordered.title: render-queue panel and output modules
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Queue items with per-item render settings and output module settings, handing execution to the shell Jobs pane.

prerequisites_ordered.title: The remaining 82 panels
prerequisites_ordered.what_to_do: Content work behind a stable registry API, fed by captured parameter metadata. Explicitly parallelisable and explicitly NOT where the risk is.

prerequisite_chain_summary: P-01 and P-02 together (module definition and viewport swap), then P-03 (centre tree). P-04 (snapshot numeric and temporal metadata) and P-05 (Affinity IL join) run in parallel behind nothing. P-05 -> P-06 (descriptor generator and UserManual seed) -> P-07 (tooltip helper) and P-08 (widen AppCommand, derive the menu). P-04 + P-08 -> P-09 (ScrubValue). P-03 + P-09 -> P-10 (dock host) -> P-11 (panel registry and spine) -> P-12 (availability predicate and slot resolver, proven through Argus). P-11 -> P-13 (document time model) -> P-14 (property tree and keyframe model in the domain layer) -> P-15 (keyframe-timeline panel) -> P-17 (graph editor). P-14 + P-09 -> P-18 (expression evaluation and inline editor) -> P-19 (expression-editor panel). P-13 + P-12 -> P-20 (clip timeline). P-20 + P-15 -> P-21 (render queue). P-16 (shortcut recomputation) runs independently and blocks only the shortcut freeze. P-22 (the remaining 82 panels) runs continuously behind P-12.

carried_gaps.title: Tool-level tooltip prose is at most 58.0% recoverable and 0% mechanically bound
carried_gaps.measured: Affinity is the ONLY captured application shipping per-tool prose: 212 explanatory sentences under [Tool summary] and [Tool description]. Against 362 canonical tools that is a 58.0% upper bound. Photoshop's .kys carries name + OSType 4CC + keystroke and nothing else; Illustrator's shortcut table carries command_id + keystroke; all 39 Premiere cmd.tools.* rows have label:null and menu_location:null; InDesign's names were regexed out of panel_strings with no adjacent description; Lightroom has no tool registry; Figma and After Effects palettes carry names and shortcuts but no prose.
carried_gaps.blocker: Serif's .NET resource keys are the neutral English source text plus a bracketed context. The join key between a tool name and its summary does not exist in the shipped strings. Same class of defect as the tool_panel_registry's own admission that id_to_name_binding is unresolved.
carried_gaps.proven_absent: 57 tools demonstrably have NO descriptive sentence: their strings appear under BOTH [Tool description] and [Tool summary] with the tool's own name as the value, because Affinity fell back to the name where no summary was written.
carried_gaps.not_dissolved_by_after_effects: The AE teardown adds 62 plain-English effect descriptions and 359 support_urls resolving to 225 distinct manual pages, but effects are not tools. The tool-level gap is unchanged.
carried_gaps.residual_after_the_prerequisite: Roughly 42% of tools will have no vendor sentence. The design must ship with that: L1 renders without the sentence rather than blocking the tip, every gap is a countable row in tooltip-gaps.json whose count is a CI gate, and authored replacements carry extraction_method=handshake_authored so authored versus derived stays countable. Hand-writing prose inside UI source files is the drift the requirement exists to prevent and is the path of least resistance under deadline; P-07 makes it a type error.

carried_gaps.title: UiTreeNode carries no numeric or temporal metadata, so OUI-008's accessibility clause is unverifiable
carried_gaps.measured: UiTreeNode is { id, author_id, node_id, role, label, value, disabled, actions, bounds, children }. It carries a string value and no numeric minimum, maximum, step or unit.
carried_gaps.consequence: argus.set_value already exists and would happily set a value that the inspector cannot check the clamp of. Every scrub control would pass CX-503D1 by being clickable while its actual numeric contract went untested - the exact class of defect the inspector exists to catch.
carried_gaps.widened_by_after_effects: The node must also carry temporal_state, time and keyframed_at_time. Without them the reported numeric_value on an animated property is a function of the playhead rather than a stored constant, and a test asserting a scrub result is unfalsifiable. 1,246 of 1,573 typed After Effects parameters are keyframable, so this is the majority case in a composition, not an edge case.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: P-04. Hard predecessor of P-09, not a follow-up.

carried_gaps.title: 142 on_hover_text calls across 24 files, zero AccessKit descriptions anywhere
carried_gaps.measured: 142 direct Response::on_hover_text calls across 24 files, no shared helper, and nothing sets an AccessKit description anywhere in the crate.
carried_gaps.consequence: Tooltip text is currently invisible to Argus. The divergence the descriptor contract exists to prevent is already present in the codebase: the tooltip string and the accessible description are two unrelated values today, and only one of them is inspectable.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: P-07. The helper is the prerequisite; the 142-site migration is scope question OQ-P.
carried_gaps.roi: The migration is mechanical and is a product-wide win, not Studio scope creep. Steps P-04, P-06 and P-07 fix an existing product-wide defect while unblocking Studio.

carried_gaps.title: GRD-001 residual: every unrebuilt menu expansion node inherits the overcount
carried_gaps.measured_where_checked: Tools: registry 1,270 against a rebuild of 353 - a 3.6x overcount. Panels: registry 814 against a dedup of 75-84 - a 9.7x overcount.
carried_gaps.unchecked_exposure: Roughly 2,630 budgeted leaves across Effects 1,230, Web Element 282, Adjustments 246, Table 152, Align & Distribute 132, Export 123, Colour Assets 110, Import 105, Shapes 85, Markers 66, Keyframes 31, OpenType 24 and Prototype Triggers 170. If those carry a comparable overcount, the true total is materially below 4,600.
carried_gaps.exempt: WORKSPACE > Tools (362) and WORKSPACE > Panels (90) only. Both were rebuilt from source.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: Either a registry re-key on (normalised name, kind, domain) with a provenance-preserving audit trail, or a per-family rebuild-from-source pass like the tools agent's, BEFORE any expansion node becomes a microtask. SAD-007's video 747 and motion 343 suggest the re-key is in progress; the re-keyed registry was not re-read for this adjudication.
carried_gaps.rule: Treat 1,533 explicit leaves as designed and every expansion figure as an upper bound.

carried_gaps.title: Shortcut arbitration was computed without After Effects
carried_gaps.measured: The 448-chord union covers Photoshop 146, Illustrator 235, Premiere 277 and Dreamweaver 185. After Effects ships 673 bindings across 32 contexts and was excluded because no shortcut capture existed at the time. InDesign remains excluded because it ships 162 shortcut categories with no key values.
carried_gaps.already_visible_conflicts: Ctrl+P breaches the frozen spine; G, W, Y, Q, C, E, U, J, K, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+T are all newly contested; five function-key bindings collide with the panel-toggle reserve. Full list in CR-17.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: P-16. Blocks freezing any shipped set, and nothing else.

carried_gaps.title: Spatial keyframe interpolation has no captured reference
carried_gaps.measured: The layer property model capture states that spatial streams carry inTangents/outTangents identifiers in the EXPRESSION vocabulary and that the shipped presets only exercise temporal interpolation.
carried_gaps.consequence: Motion-path bezier handles drawn on the canvas - the spatial half of the graph editor and the whole of on-canvas path animation - have no reference basis. Building them from memory would be exactly the speculation this green room exists to avoid.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: A targeted capture pass, or an explicitly authored design decision recorded as handshake_authored, before P-17's spatial half.

carried_gaps.title: After Effects expression argument signatures are not bound to their functions
carried_gaps.measured: 37 argument signatures are pooled in the same table as the 333 identifiers but are NOT stored adjacent to the function they belong to; the capture emits them as an ordered signature pool and explicitly refuses to assert the binding. No ExtendScript type library or header ships on disk, so return and parameter types are unrecoverable offline. 206 of the 333 identifiers precede the first category header and carry no category.
carried_gaps.consequence: Expression autocomplete and signature help have a vocabulary but no arities and no types.
carried_gaps.named_prerequisite: Either an online documentation pass or authored signatures marked handshake_authored, before the expression editor's completion features. The editor itself (P-18, P-19) is not blocked.

carried_gaps.title: Three of nine applications still have no captured menu hierarchy
carried_gaps.measured: Photoshop, Illustrator and Lightroom Classic. Down from four; After Effects is now captured. Photoshop's capture states in its own unknowns: 'No mapping exists in this install from a .kys command id to a menu path. The menu hierarchy is not present in any readable install file. UNRESOLVED', and that Photoshop.exe was not inspected. Illustrator's shortcuts file is a flat command table with no menu path field.
carried_gaps.closing_action: Photoshop's hierarchy is most likely in Photoshop.exe compiled resources. Illustrator's is likely recoverable from the .aip plugin menu registrations - illustrator_effects.json already recovered the Effect menu hierarchy that way from 105 plugins with menu registration.

carried_gaps.title: Affinity's 143 tool ids and 53 panel ids remain unbound to names
carried_gaps.measured: The capture states the 4CCs appear in the binaries only as compiled 32-bit literals and the .NET string tables are keyed by English source text, so id_to_name_binding is unresolved. It deliberately refuses to guess.
carried_gaps.consequence: Affinity's workspace STRUCTURE is reliable (which shelf, which book, how many books, which entries visible) but no claim binds a specific 4CC to a specific name.

carried_gaps.title: Lightroom Classic has no captured panel layout
carried_gaps.measured: workspaces.json is a 29-byte stub. The photo default layout is derived from lightroom_develop_parameters.json and lightroom_catalog_model.json structure plus Affinity's photo-side workspaces, not from a captured layout.
carried_gaps.status: Labelled EXTRAPOLATED_NOT_CAPTURED in the source and carried forward unchanged.

carried_gaps.title: The 240-entry synonym table is the one non-mechanical step in the tool count
carried_gaps.measured: 527 raw names normalised then collapsed through an authored 240-entry cross-vendor synonym table. Every merge ships inline as vendor_variants on each row, so any merge is visible and reversible from the artifact alone.
carried_gaps.known_debatable_merges: Photoshop's Clone Stamp merged with Affinity's Clone Brush; Illustrator's Freehand (Pencil) merged with Photoshop's Pencil although one is vector and one is raster.
carried_gaps.status: Not a blocker. Recorded so 362 is understood as an auditable judgement rather than a measurement.

carried_gaps.title: The After Effects layer type match names are only 6 of 10 confirmed
carried_gaps.measured: footage, composition, text, shape, camera and light were found on disk by match name. solid, null, adjustment and guide were NOT found and are recorded as match_names_not_found.
carried_gaps.consequence: Their existence is not in doubt - all four appear in the AE Layer menu's New submenu - but their match names are not confirmed by this capture and must not be asserted in a microtask's acceptance criteria.

open_questions.severity: architecture fork, do not resolve here
open_questions.question: Layer-based or node-based compositing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: After Effects is layer-based: a composition holds a stack of layers, each with a property tree. High-end VFX is predominantly node-based (Nuke, Fusion): a directed graph of operations. Serving 'VFX artists' properly may mean a node graph, which After Effects does not have and which the green room therefore did not capture. These are not a rendering detail; they are different document models with different undo, different parallelism and different model-steerability.
open_questions.what_the_capture_supports: The layer model fully. 1,326 match names, 759 containment edges, 13 property group topics, the keyframe record format, the expression container. A node model would need its own reference basis and has none.
open_questions.what_already_exists_in_handshake: The Loom graph surface and the canvas board in the 012 shell are node-graph precedent inside the product. Graphite (Rust, node-based, Vello-rendered) is the closest open-source field reference.
open_questions.the_weakest_form_of_the_question_that_is: A graph PROJECTION over a layer document is already required and is already field-precedented: After Effects ships Composition Flowchart and Composition Mini-Flowchart as read-only dependency views over nested compositions, and this design carries them as the comp-flowchart panel. That is a strictly weaker claim than needing a graph document model.
open_questions.status: NOT DECIDED. Surfaced as the fork it is. It changes P-14 (the domain-layer property and keyframe model) and would change the keyframe-timeline's row model, so it should be settled before P-14 rather than after.

open_questions.question: Two left rails - the shell activity rail at 32px plus Studio's Tool Rail at 44px - consume 76px before any content, and 336px with the Browse Dock expanded. Acceptable, or should Studio's tools be injected as a section INTO the shell rail? Injecting is cleaner spatially but couples Studio to shell chrome and makes the tool rail disappear when the shell rail is used for navigation.
open_questions.recommendation: Keep two rails; auto-collapse the shell rail to its 32px icon strip when ModuleId::Studio is active, which is a capability it already has. Below a width threshold auto-collapse the Browse Dock to its icon rail and surface a focus-mode command that collapses every edge in one action.

open_questions.question: The exact coarse and fine scrub modifier keys.
open_questions.recommendation: Shift coarse x10, Ctrl fine /10, Shift+Ctrl x100, Alt excluded. Reasoning and the defeated counter-argument in CR-09.

open_questions.question: Wheel default over a dense panel: does the wheel over a field step the value (with a reserved 10px scroll lane), or does the wheel always scroll with a modifier to step?
open_questions.recommendation: Keep OUI-008's stated behaviour and ship the scroll lane. The inversion is a one-line default change if the lane proves too narrow in the visual debugger.

open_questions.question: Is a 24px scrub row acceptable, or does the operator want the denser 20px vendor row with a smaller grab target? 24px costs about 20 percent of the visible parameter count per group; 20px risks missed grabs. The single biggest density lever in the design.

Do live adjustment tools (36) and live filter tools (44) stay tools, or become commands? 80 tools, 22.7% of the list, exist as tools only because Affinity models them that way; Photoshop and Illustrator model the same operations as menu items and adjustment layers.
open_questions.recommendation: Split on the gesture test: operations needing a canvas gesture to say WHERE they apply (adjustment brush, filter brush, tone brush, mask paint, the liquify set) stay tools; operations that are a parameter dialog applied to a whole layer (Levels, Curves, Posterize, Threshold, Unsharp Mask, the blurs) become commands that create a layer. That cuts 80 to roughly 14 tools plus 66 commands and lands the palette in the same size band as every reference application.
open_questions.decides: whether the distinct tool count is 362 or about 296

open_questions.question: Is preference_client.rs operator-scoped or workspace-scoped? L1 and L2 of the persistence cascade require an operator-scoped, workspace-independent store. If it is workspace-scoped it needs an operator key namespace before Studio ships.

Where does the Studio module menu band live in the AccessKit NodeId space? The shell assigns MENU_BAR_NODE_ID_BASE = 92 with fixed ids 92..=99 registered in DECLARED_IDENTITIES with a collision test, and 100 is the pane id base, so Studio's 11 module menus cannot take 100..=110. Per-module menus are also not a fixed set: Tailor, CKC and future modules will each want their own.
open_questions.recommendation: Derive module-menu title ids from author_id strings in egui's hashed space, as top_menu_bar.rs already does for dynamic LEAF nodes. That keeps the fixed band for the shell's eight and makes module menus additive without renumbering. This is a native-shell decision, not a Studio one.

open_questions.question: Is the shared asset library Loom or CKC? Spec 14.21 [STU-UNI-003] says Loom is the home for brushes, styles, palettes, components, export recipes and placed assets with no Studio-private silo. The greenroom sprint contract's operator decision says CKC (WP-KERNEL-005) is the asset library and file manager for Studio, Tailor and the future cui-studio.
open_questions.affects: FILE > Open From Asset Library, FILE > Browse Assets, FILE > Place from Asset Library, INSERT > Insert from Library, OBJECT > Component > Publish to Library, and every Libraries leaf under COLOR. Labels are written destination-neutral today.

open_questions.question: Does the Studio menu bar INSERT between the shell menus or REPLACE them while Studio has focus?
open_questions.this_design_assumes: Insert. Replace would break the fixed-NodeId contract and make GO, RUN, EDITORS and OPERATOR unreachable from the menu while a designer works.

open_questions.question: Does Studio ship generative surfaces, and if so do they route to Handshake's own ModelRuntime rather than a vendor service? The After Effects teardown excludes 8 effect surfaces, the Content-Aware Fill panel and Scene Edit Detection on an explicit AI policy, and records an on-disk MLModels store with FastMask and ShotCutDetection payloads. The Dreamweaver and Premiere captures carry the same excluded_ai policy; the Photoshop and Illustrator captures do not, and both ship generative surfaces. The tools list already carries a generative_ml family of 7.
open_questions.why_it_matters_now: If Studio routes generative work to ModelRuntime, the AI exclusion list stops being an exclusion list and becomes a re-implementation list.

open_questions.question: How many code surfaces does Studio have? The CODE menu is scoped to web-document authoring, the shell already ships an editor, and the expression editor is now a third. Where does editing a .js or .css file belonging to a Studio site actually happen, and does the expression editor share the same seam?
open_questions.this_design_assumes: One code_editor module with three framings: the shell editor, the CODE menu's web view, and the expression editor. The seam is a single leaf, CODE > Open in Shell Editor, and the expression editor reuses the module rather than the framing.

open_questions.question: How many Layout Presets ship at v1, and under what names? Twelve are proposed from the 58 shipped vendor workspace names.
How many Task Scopes ship at v1? Seven are proposed; Photoshop ships three. Each is a scoped tool set plus a scoped Tool Zone plus an exit path.

Cap of 5 auto-resolved sibling tabs in the inspector slot: is that the right number? Premiere ships a 13-tab group and After Effects ships an 11-tab group in Essential Graphics, so the platform tolerates depth, but 13 auto-generated tabs would be unreadable. The number is a judgement, not evidence.

Is migrating the existing 142 on_hover_text call sites in scope for the Studio work packet, or does Studio ship the helper and leave the legacy calls? Leaving them means AccessKit descriptions remain absent outside Studio.

Is widening AppCommand into the UiDescriptor in scope for the Studio work packet or a separate shell packet? It touches three const tables, dispatch_palette_action and the palette filter, and it benefits every module.
open_questions.decides: whether Studio is blocked on a shell change

open_questions.question: Do out-of-context menu items grey or hide? Answered here as always-grey with a machine-readable reason, but it remains listed in operator-ui-requirements.json open_for_operator_decision.

[STU-CON-007] requires every Studio tool, command and primitive to be model-invokable, parallel-safe, deterministic and visually verifiable. Does that mean every one of the 362 tools needs an Argus action and a UserManualToolEntry with a real invocation path, or is model-invokability satisfied at the command-registry level? The answer sets the floor for how much of this design is mandatory rather than desirable.

UserManualToolEntry carries ipc_channel, tauri_command, cli_flag, http_route and http_method, all of which are null for a canvas tool. Is a new page_kind or anchor_kind needed, or do canvas tools reuse the tool entry shape with null transport fields? And does a generated batch bump USER_MANUAL_VERSION once or per element? The Rust guard fails a wired-surface diff without a bump, so the generator's version behaviour must be agreed before it is written.

Which artifact or blob tier in the 012 tree does Studio bind to for bulk binary? Raster tiles, video media, brush tip bitmaps, LUTs and fonts belong in content-addressed artifact storage with SurrealDB holding the records and references. For scale: Affinity ships roughly 350 MB of brush tip bitmaps and Lightroom 854 MB of camera profiles plus 449 MB of lens profiles. Under SAD-007 video media makes this urgent rather than deferred.
open_questions.status: SAD-002 open_item, not yet verified in the 012 tree

risks.risk: The three proposals' vocabularies survive into the microtasks and the same concept is implemented twice under two names - task mode and workspace, options bar and context bar, availability and binding.
risks.mitigation: one_vocabulary.reconciliation is the authority for naming in every Studio microtask. A microtask using a superseded name is a review failure, not a style note.

risks.risk: The stale After Effects figures (481 effects, 2,001 option lists, 24 manual pages, 618 soft bounds) are carried into microtask acceptance criteria because they appear in two of the three proposals and look authoritative.
risks.mitigation: CR-06 lists every corrected figure with its measured replacement. Any microtask citing 481 effects or 2,001 option lists is reading a superseded revision.

risks.risk: ScrubValue ships without TemporalState because most documents have no timeline, and the state is retrofitted later. Retrofitting changes the widget's press-claim behaviour, which arbitration rule_1 makes load-bearing, so every gesture boundary is re-litigated at exactly the point the panels are finished.
risks.mitigation: P-09 ships TemporalState with the widget. A field that cannot say it is expression-driven cannot correctly refuse a press.

risks.risk: hard and soft bounds are collapsed into one range in the first ScrubValue commit because most low-quality sources carry only one range and one field looks sufficient until the After Effects data arrives.
risks.evidence: 366 of the 606 After Effects parameters declaring both have a soft range narrower than the legal one; Lumetri's Temperature is hard[-150,150] but ui[-100,100]; Illustrator ships a separate edit_range on 11 controls of which 9 differ.
risks.mitigation: Both fields exist in ParamSpec from the first commit even where equal, enforced by a CI check on every numeric descriptor.

risks.risk: The composition default layout is built from the panel proposal's extrapolated motion layout because that is what the deliberation artifact says, and the measured After Effects correction is missed.
risks.mitigation: CR-07 lists the five specific deltas. The composition layout in integrated_design is the measured one and the extrapolated one is explicitly superseded.

risks.risk: A shipped shortcut set is frozen before the After Effects recomputation, and Ctrl+P ships meaning two things.
risks.mitigation: P-16 blocks the freeze specifically. CR-17 lists the twelve already-visible conflicts so the recomputation has a starting point rather than a blank page.

risks.risk: The clip timeline and the keyframe timeline are built as one panel with a mode switch, because that is simpler and because After Effects appears to do it.
risks.consequence: One-at-a-time with no escape, requiring multi-instance support that does not exist. Exactly the preset-library situation SAD-006 rejected.
risks.mitigation: CR-20 states the verdict and the reason. Two panels, defaulting to two tabs in one group, with the escape available in one drag.

risks.risk: Availability filtering leaks into search, re-creating the persona problem inside the search box. Filtering unavailable results out looks like a quality improvement.
risks.consequence: The operator types a correct tool name, gets nothing, and concludes Studio does not have the tool - strictly worse than a persona toggle, which at least names the mode to switch to.
risks.mitigation: Search NEVER filters on availability; it sorts on it and displays the reason. Asserted by an inspector test that searches for a NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT element and requires a result row carrying a reason.

risks.risk: A parallel Studio command registry or a parallel Studio manual surface is created because AppCommand lacks the fields and model_manual looks like the right target.
risks.consequence: Two registries means the menu, the palette and the rail can disagree, breaking OUI-006 directly. Two manual surfaces means L2 resolves to nothing while every governance check passes.
risks.mitigation: P-06 and P-08 name the single targets explicitly, and the microtask acceptance criteria must name user_manual/store.rs row types by name.

risks.risk: Tooltip prose gets hand-written inside UI source files under deadline pressure, because 42% of tools have no recovered sentence and the blank looks like a bug.
risks.mitigation: Make it a type error: the helper accepts the generated id enum, not &str. There is no signature that takes a literal.

risks.risk: The 90-panel count is treated as a work estimate. It is a count of identities: effect-controls alone subsumes nine InDesign surfaces, Premiere's 617 effects with 9,654 parameter rows and After Effects' 635 effects with 1,573 typed records.
risks.mitigation: State it explicitly in the consuming work packet. Size from the capability corpus mapped through the panels, never from the panel count.

risks.risk: The scopes panel ships with a single-choice scope selector, and the merge silently becomes deferred debt because a colourist cannot see waveform and vectorscope at once.
risks.mitigation: CR-18 makes the internal N-up grid a same-microtask requirement, not a follow-up.

risks.risk: Five separate egui_tiles trees drift out of sync during a cross-tree drag: a tile removed from the source and never inserted into the target, losing the panel.
risks.mitigation: PanelMoveRequest applied as one transaction against the registry first, trees rebuilt from the registry, and a debug-build assertion every frame that every registered panel appears in exactly one tree.

risks.risk: The contextual inspector thrashes: every selection change reshuffles the right column, the operator loses their place, and the AccessKit tree churns so GUI tests become flaky.
risks.mitigation: Sticky active tab keyed by (profile signature, resolved primitive); resolution on selection change only, never per frame; ranks 2-5 recomputed only when rank 1 changes. Plus a validation case that selects, deselects and reselects the same node and asserts the emitted tree is byte-identical.

risks.risk: A profile signature change silently swaps the whole layout mid-edit when the operator adds a timeline to a page-layout document.
risks.mitigation: CR-08: the swap is an offer, confirmed once per document and remembered. Silent swapping is the whole-layout form of inspector thrash.

risks.risk: The Layout Preset mechanism quietly acquires gating power, because a job preset 'obviously' should not show irrelevant tools. That is the persona toggle rebuilt under a different name.
risks.mitigation: The prohibition is stated in the availability rule and is inspector-assertable: for any preset W and any element E, availability_state(E) must be identical with W active and inactive.

risks.risk: Menu-bar width. 19 top-level titles at roughly 7 characters each is about 135 characters of chrome - wider than any source application (InDesign 12, Premiere 11, Dreamweaver 10, After Effects 9). It fits 1920px, is tight at 1440px and overflows at 1280px.
risks.mitigation: An overflow chevron preserving order and still emitting every title into the AccessKit tree; abbreviated titles at narrow widths before overflow; measure at 1280/1440/1920/2560 in the visual debugger before the tree is frozen.
risks.do_not: Do not solve width by hiding inapplicable menus. That trades a rendering problem for an index-stability problem and breaks stable-target addressing.

risks.risk: The keyframe-timeline is sized by the panel_density_model and comes out too short, because that model was derived for field-dense parameter panels and a two-column tree-plus-graph panel is neither field-dense nor list-dense.
risks.mitigation: It is explicitly excluded from the mixing rule and carries its own sizing contract: 300px minimum height, 320px default and 220px minimum for the tree column, 400px floor for the time column with horizontal scroll rather than ruler compression.

risks.risk: The expression editor becomes a third code implementation because reusing code_editor is more work than embedding a text box.
risks.mitigation: [STU-SECTION-003] forbids it and P-18 names the reuse as a constraint. The seam is the same one CODE already needs, so the cost is shared rather than duplicated.

risks.risk: The After Effects double-tap reveal idiom (U/UU, E/EE) is implemented as the only path, and the out-of-process inspector cannot drive it deterministically - the same defect the tool flyout long-press was rejected for.
risks.mitigation: Every double-tap has an untimed equivalent as a menu leaf and a palette command, and the inspector targets the untimed path.

risks.risk: OQ-A (layer versus node) is deferred past P-14, and the domain-layer property and keyframe model is built assuming layers. Reversing it later means rebuilding the document model, the undo model and the keyframe-timeline row model together.
risks.mitigation: Named in OQ-A: settle it BEFORE P-14, not after. It is the one open question in this file whose cost of late resolution is a rebuild rather than a rework.

risks.risk: Vendor evidence is treated as operator evidence. What Adobe shipped as a default is not proof that the operator prefers it; it is proof of what the field converged on, which is a weaker claim.
risks.mitigation: Stated explicitly. Every placement is traceable to a counted vendor fact, and every such fact is one the operator can overrule in one drag, with L2 persistence making the overrule permanent. The defaults are a starting position, not an argument.

risks.risk: The centre editor tree being unbounded makes the persisted layout unbounded too, and a session with many groups produces an AccessKit tree that slows the inspector.
risks.mitigation: accessibility/snapshot.rs already caps snapshots at MAX_SNAPSHOT_NODES; Studio respects the cap and reports truncation explicitly rather than silently. No group cap is imposed, because OUI-002 forbids one.
